 .lh-heroalt-panel{border:1px solid #C3C9CE;border-radius:6px;background:#fff;overflow:hidden}
 .lh-heroalt-panel:hover{border-color:#E0742B}
 .lh-heroalt-card--leo{border:0;border-radius:0;background:none;padding:15px 16px 13px}
 .lh-heroalt-card--leo:hover,.lh-heroalt-card--leo:focus-visible{background:#FFFDFB;border:0}
 .lh-heroalt-kicker{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:7px;font-family:"IBM Plex Mono",ui-monospace,monospace;font-size:11.5px;letter-spacing:1.2px;text-transform:uppercase;color:#12233D;font-weight:500}
 .lh-heroalt-kicker svg{color:#E0742B;flex:0 0 auto}
 .lh-heroalt-card--leo .lh-heroalt-hint{margin-top:7px;font-size:13.5px;color:#3C4F66}
 .lh-heroalt-verified{display:flex;gap:8px;align-items:flex-start;margin:0;padding:11px 16px 13px;border-top:1px solid #EDEAE3;background:#FBF8F2;font-size:12.5px;line-height:1.5;color:#4A525C}
 .lh-heroalt-verified svg{color:#1C7A4A;flex:0 0 auto;margin-top:2px}
 /* ── Make the search the priority, not an afterthought ────────────────
 Measured before this change at 1440x900: hero 1028px tall, search bar
 top at y=694. Tightened the vertical rhythm and moved the trust row
 below, which lifts the bar roughly 230px — comfortably in view. */
 .lh-hero.lh-hero{padding:clamp(28px,4vw,56px) 0 clamp(32px,4.5vw,64px)}
 .lh-hero .lh-hero-center{gap:clamp(16px,2vw,26px)}
 /* ⚠️ THE CAUSE OF THE BIG EMPTY GAP, and it was mine. The stylesheet sets
 .lh-hero-text{flex:1 1 380px} and .lh-portals{flex:1 1 420px}. Those were
 written for the original ROW layout, where flex-basis is a WIDTH. Turning
 the container into a column silently turned both into fixed HEIGHTS: the
 text box stayed 380px tall although its content ended after 187px, and
 the search row stayed 420px tall although the cards are 195px. That is
 ~420px of enforced emptiness. Resetting the basis is the whole fix —
 never set flex-direction on an inherited flex container without checking
 what flex-basis meant before. */
 .lh-hero .lh-hero-text{flex:0 0 auto}
 .lh-hero .lh-portals--search{flex:0 0 auto}
 .lh-hero .lh-badge{margin-bottom:10px}
 .lh-hero .lh-title{margin:0 0 12px}
 .lh-hero .lh-subtitle{margin:0;max-width:52ch}
 .lh-hero .lh-trust-row{position:relative;z-index:1;margin:clamp(14px,1.8vw,22px) 0 0;gap:10px 24px}
 /* The bar itself carries the emphasis: taller, larger type, and a navy
 action instead of the yellow one — yellow reads promotional, and on warm
 paper it was the loudest thing in the hero. Scoped to .lh-herosearch so
 the same widget elsewhere keeps the brand button. */
 .lh-herosearch .sie-sps-bar{min-height:64px;padding:4px 6px 4px 14px}
 .lh-herosearch .sie-sps-input{font-size:17px}
 .lh-herosearch .sie-sps-btn{background:#12233D;border-color:#12233D;color:#fff;font-weight:600}
 .lh-herosearch .sie-sps-btn:hover{background:#1E3354;border-color:#1E3354}
 /* ── Results as a responsive grid, not a single strip ──────────────────
 .sie-res-list holds the program cards as direct children (verified live:
 18 cards, one parent, no headers in between), so one grid rule is enough.
 ⚠️ SCOPED TO THE HOMEPAGE ON PURPOSE. .sie-res-list is the shared
 SieFlowView markup — Leonardo renders into it too, with its own
 per-card animation offsets. Re-layouting it globally would change his
 results as a side effect of a homepage fix. */
 .lh-herosearch .sie-res-list{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fill,minmax(320px,1fr));gap:16px;align-items:start}
 .lh-herosearch .sie-res-list > .program-card{width:auto;max-width:none;margin:0}
 /* The flow view (AI matching on) groups results into one .sie-flow__branch
 per country. Each branch carries max-width:560px inside a 798px rail, so
 two never fit and they stack — the "single strip". Releasing the cap and
 tiling the branches gives two country panels per row at this width, and
 more on a wider screen, without touching the cards inside.
 ⚠️ Scoped to .lh-herosearch: Leonardo renders the same flow markup. */
 .lh-herosearch .sie-flow__branches{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fill,minmax(360px,1fr));gap:18px;align-items:start}
 .lh-herosearch .sie-flow__branch{max-width:none;width:100%}
 /* ── The figures strip ────────────────────────────────────────────────
 Serif numerals, monospaced labels, hairline rules, no card, no shadow,
 no colour fill behind each figure. The register of a register. */
 .lh-stats.lh-stats--figures{background:#F4F2ED;border-top:1px solid #E4E0D8;border-bottom:1px solid #E4E0D8;padding:0}
 .lh-stats--figures .lh-stats-grid{max-width:1200px;margin:0 auto;padding:0 clamp(16px,4vw,48px);display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(4,minmax(0,1fr));gap:0}
 .lh-stats--figures .lh-stat{padding:clamp(20px,2.4vw,32px) clamp(14px,2vw,28px) clamp(20px,2.4vw,32px) 0;border-right:1px solid #E4E0D8;text-align:left;background:none;border-radius:0;box-shadow:none}
 .lh-stats--figures .lh-stat:last-child{border-right:0}
 /* Every cell except the first gets inner space on its left, so each rule
 sits with equal air on both sides instead of crowding the next figure.
 The first keeps padding-left:0 so its numeral lines up with the margin
 the hero headline uses. */
 .lh-stats--figures .lh-stat + .lh-stat{padding-left:clamp(18px,2.4vw,34px)}
 .lh-stats--figures .lh-stat-num{font-family:"Source Serif 4",Georgia,serif;font-size:clamp(27px,2.9vw,40px);font-weight:600;letter-spacing:-.5px;line-height:1.05;color:#12233D;background:none;-webkit-text-fill-color:currentColor}
 /* #6B7A8D measured 3.92:1 against the warm band — under the 4.5:1 that
 11.5px text needs. The cool grey was fine on the old cold background and
 quietly failed when the palette warmed up; #4F5967 measures 6.2:1.
 Worth remembering when warming any other background. */
 .lh-stats--figures .lh-stat-label{margin-top:8px;font-family:"IBM Plex Mono",ui-monospace,monospace;font-size:11.5px;letter-spacing:1.3px;text-transform:uppercase;color:#4F5967}
 @media(max-width:700px){
 .lh-stats--figures .lh-stats-grid{grid-template-columns:repeat(2,minmax(0,1fr))}
 .lh-stats--figures .lh-stat:nth-child(2){border-right:0}
 }
 /* Monogram instead of a repeated building glyph. Hairline tile, serif
 letters — it reads as a placeholder somebody chose, not as missing data. */
 .lh-uni-logo-placeholder{display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;background:#F4F2ED;border:1px solid #E4E0D8;border-radius:5px;color:#8A8578}
 .lh-uni-monogram{font-family:"Source Serif 4",Georgia,serif;font-size:22px;font-weight:600;letter-spacing:1px;color:#12233D}
 /* ── For institutions ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
 The one full navy band on the page. It is dark on purpose: it marks a
 change of audience, so a student scrolling past knows at a glance that
 this part is not addressed to them. */
 .lh-inst{background:#12233D;color:#fff}
 .lh-inst-wrap *,.lh-inst-wrap *::before,.lh-inst-wrap *::after{box-sizing:border-box}
 .lh-inst-inner{max-width:1200px;margin:0 auto;padding:clamp(48px,6vw,88px) clamp(16px,4vw,48px);display:grid;grid-template-columns:minmax(0,1.35fr) minmax(0,1fr);gap:clamp(28px,4vw,64px);align-items:start}
 .lh-inst-badge{margin:0 0 16px;font-family:"IBM Plex Mono",ui-monospace,monospace;font-size:11.5px;letter-spacing:1.8px;text-transform:uppercase;color:#D7A83F}
 .lh-inst-h{margin:0 0 16px;font-family:"Source Serif 4",Georgia,serif;font-size:clamp(26px,3.1vw,40px);line-height:1.16;font-weight:600;letter-spacing:-.5px;color:#fff;max-width:20ch}
 .lh-inst-body{margin:0 0 26px;font-size:clamp(15.5px,1.4vw,17px);line-height:1.65;color:#C6D2E0;max-width:54ch}
 .lh-inst-actions{margin:0;display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:12px}
 .lh-inst-btn{display:inline-block;text-decoration:none;background:#fff;color:#12233D;font-size:15.5px;font-weight:600;padding:14px 26px;border:1px solid #fff;border-radius:4px;min-height:44px}
 .lh-inst-btn:hover{background:#F4F2ED;color:#12233D}
 .lh-inst-btn--ghost{background:none;color:#fff;border-color:#44597A;font-weight:500}
 .lh-inst-btn--ghost:hover{background:none;color:#fff;border-color:#D7A83F}
 .lh-inst-terms{margin:0;padding:0;list-style:none}
 .lh-inst-terms li{border-top:1px solid #28405F;padding:20px 0}
 .lh-inst-terms li:first-child{border-top:0;padding-top:0}
 .lh-inst-k{margin:0 0 6px;font-family:"IBM Plex Mono",ui-monospace,monospace;font-size:19px;color:#D7A83F}
 .lh-inst-v{margin:0;font-size:15px;line-height:1.6;color:#C6D2E0}
 @media(max-width:860px){
 .lh-inst-inner{grid-template-columns:1fr}
 }
 @media(max-width:900px){
 .lh-hero .lh-portals--search{grid-template-columns:1fr}
 .lh-herosearch .sie-res-list{grid-template-columns:1fr}
 .lh-herosearch .sie-flow__branches{grid-template-columns:1fr}
 .lh-heroalt{flex-direction:row;flex-wrap:wrap}
 .lh-heroalt-card{flex:1 1 220px}
 .lh-hero-scrim{background:linear-gradient(180deg,rgba(250,248,244,.97) 0%,rgba(250,248,244,.93) 62%,rgba(250,248,244,.72) 100%)}
 }
 /* ── Institutional pass, part 2 (2026-11-08, evening) ──────────────────
 Brings the sections below the hero onto the palette and type the hero
 already uses, so the page reads as one document instead of two designs
 stacked on top of each other. Everything here is homepage-only (it lives
 in this template) and is pure CSS: delete this block to revert. */
 /* The page itself: the site-wide body is cold pale blue (#E8F1FA), which
 showed through every transparent section (the institutions carousel and
 the study fields block) as a blue band between warm ones. */
 body.page-id-150{background:#FAF8F4}
 /* ⚠️ THE HEADLINE NEVER WAS SERIF. leonardo-homepage-css.min.css carries
 `.lh-wrap .lh-title{font-family:system-ui !important; font-size:44px
 !important; font-weight:800 !important; color:#003b73 !important}`, so
 the Source Serif rule earlier in this block lost on every device. Only
 !important with equal-or-higher specificity can beat it. */
 .lh-wrap .lh-hero .lh-title,.lh-wrap .lh-hero h2.lh-title{font-family:"Source Serif 4",Georgia,serif !important;font-weight:600 !important;font-size:clamp(34px,4.4vw,58px) !important;line-height:1.08 !important;letter-spacing:-.6px !important;color:#12233D !important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#12233D !important}
 /* The accent word: italic navy reads editorial; bright orange read promo. */
 .lh-wrap .lh-hero .lh-gradient-text{color:#12233D;-webkit-text-fill-color:#12233D;font-style:italic;font-weight:600}
 /* One label above the headline is enough. The H1 eyebrow ("STUDY IN
 EUROPE") already does that job; the extra pill only added noise. */
 .lh-hero .lh-badge{display:none}
 /* Phones: the hero had no side gutter, so the eyebrow sat flush against
 the screen edge while the centred text did not. Left-aligned, with the
 same 20px gutter as the rest of the page, it matches the desktop. */
 @media(max-width:900px){
 .lh-hero .lh-hero-center{padding-left:20px;padding-right:20px;box-sizing:border-box;text-align:left}
 .lh-hero .lh-hero-text,.lh-hero .lh-subtitle{text-align:left}
 .lh-wrap .lh-hero .lh-title{text-align:left}
 .lh-hero .lh-trust-row{justify-content:flex-start}
 }
 /* ── Section headers: same voice as the institutions band ─────────────
 Serif headings and a small monospaced label instead of the rounded blue
 pills, which were the last "app" element on the page. */
 .lh-wrap .lh-section-header h2{font-family:"Source Serif 4",Georgia,serif !important;font-weight:600 !important;font-size:clamp(28px,3vw,40px) !important;letter-spacing:-.4px;line-height:1.15;color:#12233D !important}
 .lh-wrap .lh-section-badge{display:inline-block;margin-bottom:14px;padding:0;background:none;border-radius:0;font-family:"IBM Plex Mono",ui-monospace,monospace;font-size:11.5px;font-weight:500;letter-spacing:1.8px;text-transform:uppercase;color:#8C5A23}
 .lh-wrap .lh-section-sub{color:#4A525C}
 /* Section rhythm: paper / white / paper, so each block has an edge. */
 .lh-wrap .lh-how{background:#FAF8F4}
 .lh-wrap .lh-unis{background:#fff;border-top:1px solid #E4E0D8}
 .lh-wrap .lh-dest-section--origins{background:#fff;border-top:1px solid #E4E0D8}
 /* How it works: the three steps were top-aligned, so the middle card
 (longer text) hung lower than its neighbours. Stretch evens them. */
 .lh-wrap .lh-steps{align-items:stretch}
 .lh-wrap .lh-step{background:#fff;border:1px solid #E4E0D8;border-radius:6px;box-shadow:none}
 .lh-wrap .lh-step-num{background:#12233D;font-family:"IBM Plex Mono",ui-monospace,monospace;font-weight:500}
 .lh-wrap .lh-step-icon{background:#F4F2ED;color:#12233D;border-radius:6px}
 .lh-wrap .lh-step-arrow{color:#B7B1A5}
 /* Cards: tighter corners and hairlines everywhere. */
 .lh-wrap .lh-uni-card{border-radius:6px;box-shadow:none}
 .lh-wrap .lh-dest-section--origins a[class*="card"],.lh-wrap .lh-dest-section--origins [class*="card"]{border-radius:6px;border-color:#E4E0D8;box-shadow:none}
 .lh-wrap .lh-dest-section--countries a[class*="card"],.lh-wrap .lh-dest-section--countries [class*="card"]{border-radius:6px}
 /* ── Study fields block (rendered by [sie_study_fields] after .lh-wrap) ─
 Six bright category colours, gradient pills and a gradient CTA made it
 the loudest part of the page. Same content, one navy, warm neutrals.
 The branch colours arrive as INLINE custom properties and inline
 backgrounds, so these overrides need !important to apply. Scoped to the
 homepage: the study-field pages keep their colour coding. */
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-title{font-family:"Source Serif 4",Georgia,serif;font-weight:600;font-size:clamp(28px,3vw,40px);letter-spacing:-.4px;color:#12233D}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-subtitle{color:#4A525C}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-flow__source-pill{background:#12233D !important;background-image:none !important;box-shadow:none !important;border-radius:4px}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-flow__junction-dot{background:#12233D}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-flow__branch{--branch-color:#12233D !important;--branch-bg:#F4F2ED !important;border:1px solid #E4E0D8;border-radius:6px;box-shadow:none}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-flow__branch-accent{display:none}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-flow__branch-icon{background:#12233D !important;border-radius:5px}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-flow__branch-count{background:#F4F2ED !important;color:#12233D !important}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-flow__field-card{background:#FAF8F4;border:1px solid #EDEAE3;border-radius:5px}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-flow__field-card:hover{border-color:#12233D}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-flow__field-icon{background:#F4F2ED !important;color:#12233D !important;border-radius:5px}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-flow__leo-link{color:#0B5FA5 !important}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-leonardo{background:#12233D !important;background-image:none !important;border-radius:6px}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-leo-btn{background:#fff !important;color:#12233D !important;border-color:#fff !important;border-radius:4px}
 /* Alignment: the search widget carries its own 24px side padding, so the
 bar sat indented from the headline above it; and the trust row was
 centred under a left-aligned column. Both now share the text's edge.
 Only the LEFT padding goes: removing the right one too pushed the
 "AI-enhanced matching" toggle across the seam into the navy side. */
 .lh-herosearch .sie-sps-wrap{padding-left:0 !important}
 .lh-hero .lh-trust-row{justify-content:flex-start}
 /* Institution cards: the stylesheet tints each card top a different pastel
 (blue / yellow / blue) via !important rules at .lh-uni-card:nth-child()
 specificity, so this needs one more class to win. Plain paper, so the
 monogram or logo is the only thing that differs between cards. */
 .lh-wrap .lh-uni-card:nth-child(n) .lh-uni-card-top{background:#F4F2ED !important;background-image:none !important;border-bottom:1px solid #EDEAE3}
 .lh-wrap .lh-uni-cta{color:#0B5FA5 !important}
 .lh-wrap .sie-dest-hub__name{color:#12233D}
 /* Europe silhouette on the navy side. Present, never loud: a lighter blue
 at 15% so the copy on top keeps full contrast. The right edge fades out
 because the map is cut through Russia there, and a hard vertical cut
 would read as a mistake. The stroke in the fill colour closes the
 hairline seams between neighbouring countries; opacity sits on the <svg> itself so overlapping strokes cannot add up into darker lines. */
 .lh-hero-navy{overflow:hidden}
 .lh-hero-map{position:absolute;top:6%;bottom:6%;left:6%;width:92%;height:88%;opacity:.15;pointer-events:none;-webkit-mask-image:linear-gradient(to right,#000 78%,transparent 100%);mask-image:linear-gradient(to right,#000 78%,transparent 100%)}

 DESTINATIONS PANEL  — overlay + grid
 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
 /* Outer layer: covers full viewport */
 .sie-dest-panel {
 position: fixed;
 inset: 0;
 z-index: 2147483000;
 display: flex;
 align-items: stretch;
 justify-content: flex-end;
 opacity: 0;
 visibility: hidden;
 pointer-events: none;
 transition: opacity .25s ease, visibility .25s;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel.open {
 opacity: 1;
 visibility: visible;
 pointer-events: auto;
 }
 /* Backdrop */
 .sie-dest-panel__backdrop {
 position: absolute;
 inset: 0;
 background: rgba(11, 55, 112, .52);
 backdrop-filter: blur(3px);
 -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(3px);
 cursor: pointer;
 }
 /* Sheet — right-panel on desktop */
 .sie-dest-panel__sheet {
 position: relative;
 z-index: 1;
 width: min(800px, 100%);
 height: 100%;
 background: #fff;
 overflow-y: auto;
 -webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch;
 padding: 26px 26px 40px;
 display: flex;
 flex-direction: column;
 gap: 0;
 transform: translateX(28px);
 opacity: 0;
 transition: transform .38s cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1), opacity .38s cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1);
 box-shadow: -20px 0 48px rgba(0,0,0,.18);
 }
 .sie-dest-panel.open .sie-dest-panel__sheet {
 transform: translateX(0);
 opacity: 1;
 }
 /* Mobile: bottom-sheet */
 @media (max-width: 767px) {
 .sie-dest-panel {
 align-items: flex-end;
 justify-content: stretch;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__sheet {
 width: 100%;
 height: 92vh;
 border-top-left-radius: 22px;
 border-top-right-radius: 22px;
 padding: 20px 16px 40px;
 transform: translateY(28px);
 box-shadow: 0 -16px 48px rgba(0,0,0,.18);
 }
 .sie-dest-panel.open .sie-dest-panel__sheet {
 transform: translateY(0);
 }
 }
 /* ── Header ── */
 .sie-dest-panel__header {
 display: flex;
 align-items: center;
 justify-content: space-between;
 margin-bottom: 6px;
 flex-shrink: 0;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__titlewrap {
 display: flex;
 align-items: center;
 gap: 10px;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__globe {
 font-size: 22px;
 color: #1e66f5;
 line-height: 1;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__title {
 font-size: 1.5rem;
 font-weight: 800;
 color: #0b3770;
 margin: 0;
 line-height: 1.2;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__close {
 background: transparent;
 border: 0;
 font-size: 22px;
 color: #0b3770;
 cursor: pointer;
 padding: 6px 8px;
 border-radius: 8px;
 line-height: 1;
 opacity: .75;
 transition: opacity .15s, background .15s;
 flex-shrink: 0;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__close:hover {
 opacity: 1;
 background: #f0f4ff;
 }
 /* Subheading */
 .sie-dest-panel__sub {
 color: #466087;
 font-size: .94rem;
 margin: 0 0 20px;
 flex-shrink: 0;
 }
 /* ── Country grid ── */
 .sie-dest-panel__grid {
 display: grid;
 grid-template-columns: repeat(4, 1fr);
 gap: 14px;
 /* allow this to grow and scroll */
 flex: 1;
 align-content: start;
 }
 @media (max-width: 620px) {
 .sie-dest-panel__grid {
 grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr);
 gap: 10px;
 }
 }
 @media (min-width: 621px) and (max-width: 860px) {
 .sie-dest-panel__grid {
 grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr);
 }
 }
 /* ── Country card ── */
 .sie-dest-panel__card {
 position: relative;
 display: block;
 aspect-ratio: 3 / 2;
 border-radius: 12px;
 overflow: hidden;
 text-decoration: none;
 background: #1d3557;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__card--no-img .sie-dest-panel__card-bg {
 background: linear-gradient(135deg, #1d3557 0%, #1e66f5 100%);
 }
 /* Hero image layer — scales on hover */
 .sie-dest-panel__card-bg {
 position: absolute;
 inset: 0;
 transition: transform .4s ease;
 will-change: transform;
 }
 /* <img> fills the card exactly like background-size:cover did.
 loading="lazy" means the browser only fetches each image when the
 panel opens and the card enters the viewport — saving ~30 MB of
 upfront image requests on every page that includes this panel. */
 .sie-dest-panel__card-img {
 position: absolute;
 inset: 0;
 width: 100%;
 height: 100%;
 object-fit: cover;
 object-position: center;
 display: block;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__card:hover .sie-dest-panel__card-bg,
 .sie-dest-panel__card:focus-visible .sie-dest-panel__card-bg {
 transform: scale(1.07);
 }
 /* Gradient overlay + text */
 .sie-dest-panel__card-body {
 position: absolute;
 inset: 0;
 display: flex;
 flex-direction: column;
 justify-content: flex-end;
 padding: 10px 12px 10px;
 background: linear-gradient(
 to top,
 rgba(0, 0, 0, .72) 0%,
 rgba(0, 0, 0, .30) 55%,
 transparent 100%
 );
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__card-name {

 font-weight: 700;
 font-size: .92rem;
 line-height: 1.2;

 .sie-dest-panel__card-arrow {

 margin-top: 2px;
 transition: color .2s ease, transform .2s ease;
 line-height: 1;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__card:hover .sie-dest-panel__card-arrow,
 .sie-dest-panel__card:focus-visible .sie-dest-panel__card-arrow {
 color: rgba(255,255,255,.9);
 transform: translateX(4px);
 }

 body.sie-dest-panel-open {

 top: 8px;
 right: 8px;
 z-index: 10;
 background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.88);

 border-radius: 20px;
 padding: 4px 8px 4px 7px;
 display: flex;
 align-items: center;
 gap: 4px;
 cursor: pointer;
 font-size: 13px;
 color: #94a3b8;
 box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,.22);
 backdrop-filter: blur(6px);
 -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(6px);

 justify-content: center;

<div class="ecl"><h2><strong>What is the Conference?</strong></h2>

<p>The <strong>Conference on the Future of Europe </strong>is the first transnational discussion with Europeans on how to address Europe’s challenges together. This is an opportunity to think about what citizens and&nbsp; civil society want for the European Union.</p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

  <div class="eac-body lc-stripe-wrapper-text"><h2><strong>How does the Conference work?</strong></h2>

<p>Europeans can share ideas via the <a href="https://futureu.europa.eu/?locale=en" target="_blank" class=" eac-external-link">Multilingual Digital Platform</a>, and both national and&nbsp;<a href="https://futureu.europa.eu/assemblies/citizens-panels" target="_blank" class=" eac-external-link">European Citizens' Panels</a>. These contributions feed into the&nbsp;<a href="https://futureu.europa.eu/pages/plenary" target="_blank" class=" eac-external-link">Conference Plenaries</a>.</p>

<p>The Conference&nbsp;offers a new public forum for an open, inclusive, and transparent debate with citizens around a number of key priorities and challenges.</p>

<h2><strong>How can you participate?</strong></h2>

<ul>
	<li><!--[if !supportLists]--><!--[endif]--><a href="https://futureu.europa.eu/processes?locale=en&amp;pk_source=pdf_document&amp;pk_medium=link&amp;pk_campaign=europarl" target="_blank" class=" eac-external-link">share your own ideas or support others’ ideas</a> on the multilingual digital Conference platform</li>
	<li><!--[if !supportLists]--><!--[endif]-->organise your own events and promote it by adding them to the <a href="https://futureu.europa.eu/?locale=en&amp;pk_source=pdf_document&amp;pk_medium=link&amp;pk_campaign=europarl" target="_blank" class=" eac-external-link">Conference platform</a></li>
	<li><!--[if !supportLists]--><!--[endif]-->take a look at the <a href="https://futureu.europa.eu/meetings" target="_blank" class=" eac-external-link">events organised by people across the EU</a></li>
</ul>

<h2><strong>What will the outcome be?</strong></h2>

<p>All of the ideas gathered and reports on events are published on the platform openly and transparently. These reports will then directly influence the discussions in the European Citizens’ Panels as well as in the Plenaries, where citizens will enter into a dialogue with national and European decision makers.</p>

<p>By spring 2022, the Conference will provide guidance on the future of Europe to the European institutions</p>

<p><a href="https://futureu.europa.eu/pages/getinvolved" target="_blank" class=" eac-external-link">Get involved and make your voice heard when it comes to education, culture, youth, sport, and more</a>.</p>

          Das ISD ist ein globaler Think-and-Do-Tank, der sich dem Schutz von Demokratie und Menschenrechten widmet und L\u00f6sungen gegen instrumentalisierten Hass, Polarisierung, Desinformation und Extremismus weltweit entwickelt. Das ISD verbindet Forschung und Analyse mit Regierungsberatung sowie der Konzeption und Durchf\u00fchrung internationaler Trainings-, Bildungs- und Kommunikationsprogramme, um evidenzbasierte Antworten auf diese Herausforderungen umzusetzen. Die ISD-Teams sind in London, Amman, Berlin und Washington, DC angesiedelt.<\/span><\/p>

          <\/p>

          Warum f\u00fcr das ISD arbeiten?<\/span><\/strong><\/p>

          Das ISD ist kein gew\u00f6hnlicher Think Tank. Wir verwandeln Forschung in Ma\u00dfnahmen, die die Welt ver\u00e4ndern. Unsere Erkenntnisse verstauben nicht in Schubladen, sie st\u00e4rken den Kampf f\u00fcr Demokratie und Menschenrechte an vorderster Front. Wir setzen uns daf\u00fcr ein, echten Wandel zu bewirken, vom lokalen bis zum globalen Niveau. Wir suchen engagierte Menschen, die unsere Leidenschaft teilen, einen Unterschied zu machen. Werde Teil einer Organisation, die wirkliche Wirkung erzielt.<\/span><\/p>

          Die Leitprinzipien des ISD \u2013 <\/span>Integrit\u00e4t, Zusammenarbeit, Flexibilit\u00e4t und Courage<\/span><\/strong> \u2013 pr\u00e4gen, wer wir als Team und Organisation sind. Diese Prinzipien spiegeln unsere Kultur wider und leiten unser Handeln und unsere Entscheidungen.<\/span><\/p>

          <\/p>

          \u00a0Unsere Benefits<\/span><\/strong><\/p>

          • Flexibles Arbeiten mit Home-Office nach Prinzipien von Vertrauen, Kommunikation und Flexibilit\u00e4t.<\/span><\/p><\/li>

          • Gro\u00dfz\u00fcgige Urlaubsregelungen.<\/span><\/p><\/li>

          • 1 zus\u00e4tzliche Woche bezahlter Urlaub \u00fcber Weihnachten, zus\u00e4tzlich zum regul\u00e4ren Urlaubsanspruch.<\/span><\/p><\/li>

          • Home-Office-Zuschuss<\/span><\/p>

            <\/p><\/li><\/ul>

            Gehalt<\/span><\/strong><\/p>

            \u20ac18 brutto pro Stunde<\/span><\/p>

            <\/p>

            Arbeitsort<\/span><\/strong><\/p>

            Der Arbeitsort kann unser B\u00fcro in Berlin sein oder in einer hybriden Arbeitsform nach Absprache. Die Bewerber*innen m\u00fcssen \u00fcber eine <\/span>Arbeitsberechtigung f\u00fcr Deutschland<\/span><\/strong> verf\u00fcgen. Eine Visa-Sponsoring-M\u00f6glichkeit besteht f\u00fcr diese Stelle nicht.<\/span><\/p>

            <\/p>

            Vertragsart<\/span><\/strong><\/p>

            Start: 04.01.2027; befristet bis 31.12.2027; Teilzeit 20 Stunden pro Woche<\/span><\/p>

            <\/p>

            Gleichberechtigung, Vielfalt und Inklusion<\/span><\/strong><\/p>

            ISD verpflichtet sich zur F\u00f6rderung von Diversit\u00e4t in der gesamten Belegschaft und strebt ein Team an, das die Gesellschaft in all ihren Facetten widerspiegelt. Wir setzen alles daran, dass unser Arbeitsplatz, unsere Personalpolitik und unsere Organisationskultur ein inklusives, positives und fortschrittliches Umfeld schaffen, in dem alle Teammitglieder mit W\u00fcrde und Respekt behandelt werden. F\u00fcr weitere Informationen zu dieser Richtlinie oder unseren Rekrutierungspraktiken kontaktieren Sie bitte <\/span>.<\/span><\/p>

            <\/p>

            Wir begr\u00fc\u00dfen besonders Bewerbungen von People of Color, Personen der LGBTQ+-Community, Menschen mit Behinderungen, neurodivergente Personen, Pflegepersonen und Menschen aus unterschiedlichen sozio\u00f6konomischen Hintergr\u00fcnden.<\/span><\/p>

            <\/p>

            Deine Aufgabe:<\/span><\/strong><\/p>

            Wir suchen ab sofort eine*n engagierte*n Werkstudent*in Communications & Social Media, der*die unser Kommunikationsteam in Berlin unterst\u00fctzt. Du berichtest an unsere*n Senior Communications Consultant und arbeitest eng mit Kolleg*innen aus den Analysis-, Advisory- und Action-Teams des ISD zusammen.<\/span><\/p>

            <\/p>

            Deine Hauptaufgabe ist es, daf\u00fcr zu sorgen, dass die Forschung des ISD Germany m\u00f6glichst viel Wirkung entfaltet. Dazu geh\u00f6ren: Beitr\u00e4ge und Datenvisualisierungen f\u00fcr die Website von ISD Germany erstellen, unsere Social-Media-Kan\u00e4le betreuen sowie Medienanfragen und Medienkontakte managen. Dabei achtest du darauf, dass unsere Kommunikation zeitlich gut mit politischen Ereignissen, Nachrichtenlagen und Ver\u00f6ffentlichungsterminen abgestimmt ist. Au\u00dferdem unterst\u00fctzt du bei der Pflege unseres CRM-Systems monday.com, wirkst an laufenden Projekten der verschiedenen ISD-Entit\u00e4ten mit und bist Schnittstelle zwischen unterschiedlichen Teams.<\/span><\/p>

            <\/p>

            Voraussetzungen: F\u00fcr eine T\u00e4tigkeit als Werkstudent*in ist es notwendig, dass du aktuell an einer Hochschule eingeschrieben bist und eine g\u00fcltige Immatrikulationsbescheinigung vorlegen kannst.<\/span><\/p>

            <\/p>


            Verantwortlichkeiten <\/span><\/strong><\/p>

            1. Kommunikationsoutputs<\/span><\/strong><\/p><\/li><\/ol>

              • Entwicklung und Weiterentwicklung von Kommunikationsformaten f\u00fcr LinkedIn und andere Social-Media-Kan\u00e4le<\/span><\/p><\/li>

              • Verfassen, Abstimmen und Ver\u00f6ffentlichen von Beitr\u00e4gen f\u00fcr Social Media<\/span><\/p><\/li>

              • CMS-Management, Pflege und Aktualisierung der Website<\/span><\/p><\/li>

              • Entwicklung von Websiteformaten, Newsletter und ggf. einer Substack-Pr\u00e4senz in Absprache mit dem*der Senior Communications Consultant<\/span><\/p><\/li>

              • Verfassen, Abstimmen und Ver\u00f6ffentlichen von Blogposts<\/span><\/p><\/li>

              • Anlegen und Ver\u00f6ffentlichen regelm\u00e4\u00dfiger Analyseformate und Forschungsergebnisse<\/span><\/p><\/li>

              • Bearbeitung von Medienanfragen und Platzierung der Forschungsergebnisse von ISD Germany in den Medien<\/span><\/p><\/li><\/ul>

                <\/p>

                2. Datenvisualisierung<\/span><\/strong><\/p>

                • Erstellung von Datenvisualisierungen f\u00fcr unterschiedliche Kommunikationsprodukte, darunter Pr\u00e4sentationen, E-Mails und Berichte<\/span><\/p><\/li>

                • Datenvisualisierungen f\u00fcr Social Media und Website<\/span><\/p><\/li>

                • Unterst\u00fctzung bei der Erstellung monatlicher E-Mails mit Forschungsergebnissen f\u00fcr wichtige Stakeholder<\/span><\/p>

                  <\/p><\/li><\/ul>

                  3. Daten- und Kontaktmanagement \/ Administration<\/span><\/strong><\/p>

                  • Organisation von und Teilnahme an ausgew\u00e4hlten Meetings<\/span><\/p><\/li>

                  • Nachverfolgung und Dokumentation von Medienengagement in <\/span>monday.com<\/span><\/a><\/p><\/li>

                  • Aktualisierung von Publikationskalendern<\/span><\/p><\/li>

                  • Unterst\u00fctzung bei laufenden Projekten der verschiedenen ISD-Entit\u00e4ten (z. B. projektspezifische Newsletter)<\/span><\/p><\/li><\/ul>

                    <\/p>

                    Dein Profil <\/span><\/strong><\/p>

                    • Du bist an einer Hochschule eingeschrieben.<\/span><\/p><\/li>

                    • Du teilst die Mission des ISD und interessierst dich f\u00fcr sozialen Zusammenhalt, die Pr\u00e4vention von gewaltbereitem Extremismus und\/oder Desinformation.<\/span><\/p><\/li>

About Us

At Onterris, we build careers grounded in purpose, responsibility and real-world impact.

“For Planet and Progress” is our north star that guides everything we do. We believe environmental responsibility and human progress are interconnected, interwoven and international. Our scientists, engineers, field teams, consultants and professionals collaborate across disciplines and geographies, guiding industries and governments, ensuring that communities and environments thrive.

When you join us, you’re not just forging a career, you’re joining a movement. A movement for better thinking, smarter solutions and lasting impact.

Together, we will advance our way of life and protect the integrity of our environment every step of the way.

A Day in the Life

As an Environmental Health Scientist – Air Quality, you’ll report to the Director of Integrated Environmental Health within the Health Sciences division at Onterris. You will support a diverse portfolio of environmental projects involving air quality permitting, regulatory compliance, air dispersion modeling, and environmental risk assessment. The ideal candidate will have a strong technical background in air quality and environmental sciences, practical experience navigating federal and state environmental regulations, and the ability to manage projects and deliver high-quality technical work for clients across various industries. The successful applicant will be a well-organized self-starter with 3-5 years of experience in air quality and/or risk assessment including at least 2 years in a consulting environment. This is an excellent opportunity for an environmental professional who enjoys solving complex regulatory and technical challenges, working directly with clients and regulatory agencies, and contributing to the successful execution of consulting projects across the team. While the majority of day-to-day life will be completed in-office (or remote), opportunities to complete site visits and attend client meetings may arise.

The compensation range for this role is $100,000 to $120,000 in addition to eligibility for an annual bonus (up to 12%) based on personal, department, and company performance. The compensation range is commensurate with experience, skillset, and geographic location.

To thrive in this role, you’ll be comfortable taking ownership of the following responsibilities:

  • Manage the full life-cycle of air quality and health risk consulting projects within the Integrated Environmental Health team, serving a diverse portfolio of industrial and commercial clients. Coordinate project schedules, budgets, deliverables and resource allocation.
  • Prepare and manage air quality permit applications and interpret and apply applicable federal, state, and local environmental regulations including Clean Air Act requirements. Evaluate regulatory applicability and compliance obligations for industrial facilities and other regulated sources.
  • Conduct air dispersion modeling using applicable EPA-approved methodologies, such as AERMOD. Translate the data into clear, defensible assessments of potential public health implications, partnering with toxicologists, risk assessors, and industrial hygienists to communicate findings to clients and regulators.
  • Collaborate effectively with project managers and multidisciplinary teams to communicate project status, identify technical challenges, manage priorities, and support the successful execution of multiple concurrent projects.
  • Develop and sustain strong, trusted relationships with clients, regulatory agencies, and internal team members through timely communication, technical support, and outstanding client service at every stage of the project life-cycle.

Your Expertise and Skills

These requirements reflect the knowledge, skills and abilities that help you do your best work here.

  • Ability to travel up to 15%
  • Ability to interface with cross-functional teams and all levels of personnel/management
  • Academic degree in Environmental Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Environmental Science, Chemistry, Toxicology, Public Health or other related engineering or science discipline
  • 3 – 5 years of related experience in air quality and/or risk assessment, including at least 2 years in a consulting environment
  • Working knowledge of federal, state and local air quality regulations and permitting programs, with experience performing emissions calculations
  • Proficiency in EPA-approved air dispersion models and health risk assessment concepts, with the ability to interpret modeled results against health-based criteria
  • Ability to work independently and with minimal supervision
  • ·Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships within a matrix reporting structure

Work Environment and Physical Requirements (Optional to Include)

The physical and environmental requirements below reflect what’s typically needed to perform the essential functions of this role safely and effectively. We may provide reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities, consistent with applicable law, to support performance of the essential functions.

  • Sitting, standing, and walking
  • Lifting 50 pounds several times a day

Company Overview

Our client makes inspection software for property managers. It has a mobile field app, a web dashboard, reports and integrations, plus an AI that turns a spoken walkthrough into a report. The app captures geotagged photos, video and voice offline and syncs later.

The founder started the company in 2014, after trying to capture thousands of photos fast during mass move-outs in a college town. It's bootstrapped and profitable, and it grows through direct sales, referrals and partnerships. The team is fully remote and writes things down, and the CEO sets priorities with you directly.

Your Role

As Product Specialist, you'll own the path from a customer's problem to a tested release and its written notes. You'll write requirements, test features by hand, and keep engineering work on dates through clear follow-up.

You'll report to the Head of Product Engineering and work with Support, Customer Success, Marketing and the CEO. This is an individual contributor seat with no direct reports. The role is fully remote, with overlap with Pacific hours.

Success means engineers build from your requirements and their questions are about edge cases. Every roadmap item you follow has an owner, a date and a written decision. Within 6 to 12 months, you run the whole path from customer problem to release notes on your own.

You'll

  • Talk with customers and read Support trends to find where workflows break
  • Write requirements with edge cases for engineering to build from
  • Test each feature on a phone, from capture and offline sync to the final report
  • Send findings to engineering as steps, expected result and actual result
  • Trace repeated support tickets to their root cause, then confirm the fix stopped them
  • Prepare releases with Marketing and Support and check draft notes against the feature
  • Ask engineering for dates, check progress and raise risks as soon as you see them
  • Use AI to summarize customer feedback and draft first versions of requirements

You Bring

  • 3+ years in SaaS product, product ops, program or project management, QA, or implementation
  • Hands-on testing of a mobile or web product, and writing up what broke
  • Written requirements, specs or user stories with edge cases that developers built from
  • Daily use of AI tools for real work, with something you built and can demo
  • Clear written English for a US team
  • A tracker you kept current across several teams, chasing late items yourself
  • Self-direction in a small remote team with little process
  • Availability for Pacific hours

Bonus Points

  • Time in property management, field service or inspections
  • Release notes, help articles or FAQs you wrote for customers
  • A prototype you built with an AI coding tool
  • Testing a mobile app that captures offline and syncs later

What's Offered

  • Compensation based on experience and where you're based. Share your target range and we'll go from there.

Interview Process

1️⃣ First call: 30 minutes with us at atomic✳HR on what you have built, working terms and what you want next.
2️⃣ Practical exercise: you analyze a workflow and write the requirements for it, the same work the seat does each week. It shows how you find edge cases and how clearly you write for an engineer.
3️⃣ Team interview: a conversation with team members on how you would work across customers, Support, Marketing and engineering, and how you follow up when work stalls.
4️⃣ Conversation with the Head of Product Engineering: your future manager, on how you would work with engineering as it moves toward services, how you hold delivery to dates, and how you write down decisions.
5️⃣ Final with the CEO: what you would own, how you keep work moving, and how you use AI day to day.

The company integrates the enterprise platforms utilities run on, including asset management, ERP and cloud systems, and deploys grid modernization frameworks. It is an active member of a leading industry alliance for utility energy-data standards.

Its platforms are already live with North American utilities. Recent deployments include an eMobility platform that manages EV onboarding, charging networks and energy marketplaces, and a workforce automation platform that shortens storm and outage restoration times.

With North American operations expanding quickly, the company is investing in senior US leadership to scale its AI practice.

The opportunity

Our client is seeking a hands-on, client-facing AI leader to help utilities move from experimentation to enterprise-scale AI. This role sits at the intersection of technology, domain expertise and client advisory, shaping how utilities design, govern and scale AI across their operations.

In this role, you will be a trusted AI advisor to utility customers, combining deep technical expertise with a strong understanding of the utility business. You will build and demo proofs of concept, lead workshops and presentations, shape proposals, and help clients move from experimentation to AI in production. You will work closely with sales leaders, executives and domain experts across the utility value chain, and help build partnerships across the AI ecosystem.

This is a builder's role in a consulting model: you will design, sell and deliver. As the practice grows, so will the team around you.

What you'll do
  • Lead the development and deployment of AI/ML and Vertical AI solutions for Energy and Utilities.
  • Support the AI product vision, prioritize use cases and execute against roadmap priorities aligned to business value.
  • Translate insights into product requirements, user stories, success metrics and launch plans.
  • Serve as a business and technical leader for model architecture, feature engineering, training pipelines and inference services.
  • Oversee model validation, explainability, bias testing and audit readiness.
  • Collaborate with product and business leaders to translate use cases into scalable AI features.
  • Build proofs of concept, demo them to customers and iterate toward production solutions.
  • Advise utilities on scaling AI across the enterprise, including infrastructure, security and governance.
  • Engage customers through presentations, workshops, conferences and proposals.
  • Build partnerships with leading AI platform and cloud providers.
  • Build deep, trusted partner relationships with clients and partners, co-innovating on Energy and Utilities AI use cases and those from similar industries.
  • Work with clients and partners on operations and business strategy: measuring innovation and satisfaction, understanding challenges and offering help when needed.
  • Provide thought leadership and innovation, with the confidence to challenge business strategy with the client.
​

Core AI concepts and technologies
  • Machine learning and modeling:supervised, unsupervised and reinforcement learning; deep learning (CNNs, RNNs, Transformers); NLP and LLMs; generative AI (diffusion models, fine-tuning, RAG).
  • AI engineering and MLOps:model training, deployment, monitoring and retraining; feature stores, vector databases and model registries; CI/CD pipelines for ML; GPU and accelerator compute architectures.
  • Cloud and infrastructure:Azure AI and Azure ML, AWS SageMaker or Google Vertex AI; Kubernetes, containerization and microservices; data platforms such as Databricks, Snowflake and Synapse.
  • Responsible AI and governance:model explainability (SHAP, LIME); fairness, bias detection and model risk controls; privacy-preserving ML (differential privacy, federated learning).
  • Programming and tooling:Python, PyTorch, TensorFlow, JAX; LangChain, semantic search and vector embeddings; prompt engineering and LLM orchestration frameworks.
​

Requirements

What you bring​
  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science or a related field.
  • 12+ years of overall industry experience, with Energy sector exposure preferred.
  • 5–8 years of experience in AI/ML or data science.
  • Hands-on experience deploying AI in large enterprises, preferably utilities, including the infrastructure and architecture needed to scale it (e.g., on Azure).
  • Prior experience working in, or consulting to, the utilities industry is preferred.
  • Experience working with large-scale operational or transactional data is preferred.
  • Comfortable presenting to customers and at conferences, and able to influence business strategy and communicate effectively at all levels.
  • Able to understand client challenges from both business and technology perspectives, and to independently develop client accounts.
  • Excellent communication, problem-solving and project management skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively and follow through on outcomes.
  • Embodies the values of excellence, ownership, collaboration and integrity.
  • Willingness to travel for customer and industry engagements, starting around 20% and growing with the practice.
  • Must be legally authorized to work in the United States.

Benefits

Compensation and benefits
  • Base salary: Highly competitive and commensurate with experience
  • Variable pay: performance-based variable compensation, with details shared during the initial conversation.
  • Benefits: comprehensive health coverage (medical, dental and vision), 401(k) and paid time off.

Our client offers an attractive, flexible compensation package for the right leader. Full details will be discussed during the initial conversation.

How to apply

Interested leaders are invited to apply through the HYREON careers page or connect with us directly on LinkedIn. All inquiries and applications are treated in the strictest confidence, and no information will be shared with our client without your consent.

Our client is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, pregnancy, age, national origin, disability status, genetic information, protected veteran status or any other characteristic protected by law.

Job Description Summary

This role sets the standard for paid search across Global Markets and delivers it hands-on. Building on the strong foundation our zones and agencies have established, you will work with zone marketers, agencies, and corporate and segment teams to raise the quality and consistency of search marketing across our markets. For some zones you will design and run campaigns. For others you will guide the zone or its agency.

You will also partner closely with Corporate Marketing and business teams to run test-and-learn programs in answer engine optimization (AEO) and generative engine optimization (GEO).

Job Description

Core responsibilities

  • Search standards. Define and maintain global standards for paid search, including account structure, keyword and bidding approach, structured testing, campaign taxonomy, UTM and conversion tracking, and brief and intake requirements. Drive adoption across zones that use different delivery models.
  • Enablement. Train zone marketers and agencies on the standard, share best practices and run a search community of practice.
  • Hands-on execution. For campaigns you run, lead advanced keyword strategy, ad creation, bidding, structured A/B and multivariate testing, audience targeting and landing page optimization. Quality-check tracking and ad delivery.
  • Measurement. Define search performance reporting. Work with analytics teams to apply attribution models and track key performance indicators (KPIs), including click-through rate, conversion rate, cost per acquisition (CPA) and return on ad spend (ROAS). Present results clearly to stakeholders in and outside marketing.
  • Budget stewardship. Own and forecast central search budgets. Manage zone- and business-funded budgets for campaigns you run, and advise on those you guide. Track pacing and planned-versus-actual spend across budgets, and flag over- and underspend. Optimize for return on investment and scalability. Identify wasted spend through negative keyword and audience refinement, and reinvest the savings in higher-performing search.
  • AEO and GEO. Lead test-and-learn programs and document what you learn. You will influence, but not own, site and content decisions.
  • Multi-market delivery. Adapt search strategy across languages, currencies and regional platform behavior.
  • Collaboration. Work with Corporate Marketing (SEO and web), segment and product teams, and agencies to connect search to customer lifecycle programs. Coordinate with other digital channel teams, such as social, to support a multichannel approach.
  • Trendspotting. Track platform changes, AI capabilities in search and industry best practices, and bring them into the standard.
  • Additional responsibilities as assigned.

How you will work with zones

Zones activate search in different ways: some locally, some through their own agencies. You will adapt to each zone's model, working in one of two modes agreed with the zone.

•Lead execution. You design, launch and optimize search campaigns for one or more zones, applying the global standard directly.

•Guide and support. The zone or its agency runs its own campaigns. You provide the standard, review, benchmarking and expert guidance.

In both modes, you are accountable for the search standard and for measuring performance against it.


Qualifications

Required

  • 6–8 years in paid search, with at least 3 years in a strategy role (Mandatory)
  • Advanced English proficiency
  • Bachelor's degree in marketing, business or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • Evidence of leading adoption of AI-enabled bidding or campaign types on Google and Bing.
  • Advanced proficiency in Google Ads and GA4, and experience with an enterprise bid-management platform and an enterprise analytics or business intelligence tool.
  • Track record of improving cost per acquisition (CPA), return on ad spend (ROAS) or conversion quality, and of linking search to revenue outcomes.
  • Experience influencing senior stakeholders without formal authority.
  • Clear communicator who can present to both technical and nontechnical audiences.
  • Working knowledge of SEO and how paid and organic search complement each other.
  • Experience managing and activating paid search campaigns across multiple countries, languages and currencies, with an understanding of how local regulations, privacy requirements and market differences influence campaign setup and execution.
  • Current Google Ads Search and Google Ads Measurement certifications.

Preferred

  • Business-to-business, healthcare or other regulated-industry search experience.
  • Current Google AI-Powered Performance Ads certification.


Additional Information

Relocation Assistance Provided: No

      <region>Anywhere in the World</region>
      <category>Back-End Programming</category>
      <description><img src="https://we-work-remotely.imgix.net/logos/0171/6696/logo.gif?ixlib=rails-4.0.0&w=50&h=50&dpr=2&fit=fill&auto=compress" />

<p>
  <strong>Headquarters:</strong> New Jersey, USA
    <br /><strong>URL:</strong> <a href="https://vertican.com">https://vertican.com</a>
</p>

<h2>About the role</h2>
<p>For 40 years Vertican has buildt software that runs law firms. One year ago we created a new modern AI platform for document automation (processing/extraction/redacting) which our customers have been adopting faster than any product we've ever had. Our suite of AI-enabled products save customers thousands of hours each week by processing high volumes of documents with precision and speed.The AI team is growing and we'd like you to join.</p>
<p>We are hiring an engineer to own the document processing pipelines end to end: design, benchmarking, experimenting with new architectures and tools, threshold required for deploying a new pipeline, etc.</p>
<p>We believe it's important to build our own tooling to help us run, improve, and measure our applications. Therefore, the ideal candidate thinks outside the box on how to not just build the product/pipeline, but also the tooling needed around it.</p>
<p>You will be the first dedicated ML hire on the product taking over from the engineering manager who build the current solution and will work directly with the founding engineering team.</p>
<p>This is a senior, hands-on individual-contributor role, but we are small team and you'll be involved in design, planning, roadmapping, and architectural decisions.</p>
<h2>What you will do</h2>
<p><strong>Design the pipelines.</strong> Own the architecture of the extraction-to-posting pipelines: page classification, field extraction, candidate retrieval, claim matching, confidence gating and the hand-off to human review, etc. Decide where rules end and models begin, and what each stage must guarantee to the next, what the separation of concerns are, etc.</p>
<p>We have different pipelines for different document types and expect that at any given point in time we may have new ones emerge and may consolidate others.</p>
<p><strong>Evaluate new systems before we adopt them.</strong> Run structured trials of candidate components and recommend what to keep. Examples include probabilistic record linkage (Splink), Azure AI Content Understanding and Document Intelligence, Azure OpenAI and Foundry-hosted models, and LLM agents with tools. Similarly, test new models with the existing pipeline as they are relased from the frontier labs.</p>
<p><strong>Build the evaluation process.</strong> You'll own the process of evaluating false positives, false negatives, errors of ommission, etc, that we ultimately use to determine if we should upgrade the pipeline.&nbsp;</p>
<p><strong>Ship and operate.</strong> Take components from trial to production in our python workers on the cloud, instrument them, watch cost and quota, and diagnose the cases reviewers send back.</p>
<p><strong>Set direction.</strong> Work with leadereship on the planing for accuracy, cost improvement, and overall product improvements.</p>
<h2>What we are looking for</h2>
<p><strong>Required</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>6+ years building ML or data-intensive systems, at least 3 of them owning a production pipeline whose output people acted on.</li>
<li>Solid backend engineering understanding and ideally cloud architecture understanding.</li>
<li>Ideally hands-on experience with document understanding: OCR or layout models, field extraction from scanned PDFs, or intelligent document processing products.</li>
<li>Experience with entity resolution or record linkage at scale (Splink, Dedupe, Zingg, or your own blocking-and-scoring system) against databases of hundreds of thousands of rows.</li>
<li>You have designed an evaluation from scratch: built a labeled ground-truth set, chosen the metrics, and defended a threshold to a non-technical stakeholder.</li>
<li>Production experience with LLM APIs, including structured output, tool calling and cost or rate-limit management; you can say when an LLM is the wrong tool.</li>
<li>Strong Python and SQL. Comfortable reading Postgres query plans and writing the raw query when the ORM gets in the way.</li>
<li>Engineering/Scientist mindset: you are scientific about testing the pipeline and how results are interpeted/presented.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Nice to have</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Azure AI services (Content Understanding, Document Intelligence, Azure OpenAI, Foundry) or the AWS and GCP equivalents.</li>
<li>Financial document processing: checks, remittance advices, lockbox files, payment matching, or accounts receivable automation.</li>
<li>Exposure to collections, legal operations or other regulated workflows handling PII.</li>
<li>Probabilistic matching theory (Fellegi-Sunter) or active-learning labeling workflows.</li>
<li>Experience building human-review tooling or feedback loops that feed back into training and evaluation data.</li>
</ul>
<h2>How we work and what we offer</h2>
<p>Small team, direct access to large datasets, weekly planning, daily standup, everyone remote in US timezones.</p>
<p>What we offer:</p>
<ul>
<li>A small team of tight-knit, like-minded people passionate about high quality software</li>
<li>Competitive compensation, commensurate with a senior individual-contributor role.</li>
<li>Monthly payments in USD</li>
</ul>
<p>Vertican is an equal opportunity employer. We hire on merit and do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability or veteran status.</p>

<p>Overview</p><p>A fast-growing AI evaluation company is building expert-level benchmarks that test how well AI agents handle real professional work in the terminal. We are hiring cryptography experts to turn real, paid tasks from their own work into end-to-end challenges for AI agents, each with a working solution and a check that proves the result is correct.</p><p>***THIS IS A TASK BASED COMPENSATION MODEL. PLEASE CHECK THE APPLICATION QUESTIONS FOR MORE DETAILS.***</p><p>Responsibilities</p><p>• Design expert-level Terminal-Bench cryptography tasks by turning real, paid work from your own experience into challenges that an AI agent must solve end to end.</p><p>• Define the task environment, including files, systems, ciphertexts and data, so the challenge is realistic, self-contained and reproducible in a Linux command-line setup.</p><p>• Write a working reference solution in Python or SageMath that proves the task is solvable, for example by recovering a key or decrypting a secret.</p><p>• Build automated checks and tests that objectively verify the final result is correct, and explain how a mistake or a partial answer would be detected.</p><p>• Calibrate task difficulty so a typical expert needs about 60-75 minutes to solve it, keeping it hard for AI agents while still fair and unambiguous.</p><p>• Package each task with Docker and Git where applicable, document instructions clearly, and revise based on reviewer feedback until it meets the required quality bar.</p><p>Skills/Experience</p><p>• 3+ years of hands-on cryptanalysis or applied cryptography; GRC, audit-only, policy, sales or management roles do not count, nor does coursework only</p><p>• Did the work in the last 3 years and can name the systems, tools, data and rules used</p><p>• Uses the low-level tools of the subfield, such as SageMath and Python, and works comfortably on the Linux command line</p><p>• Can show how a finding is proven, such as a decrypted secret or a recovered key, and explain how a mistake would be caught</p><p>• Technical fluency with files, CSV/JSON, APIs or databases</p><p>• Available to start around November 2026</p><p>Nice-to-have</p><p>• Published write-ups or research on cryptanalysis</p><p>• Strong CTF results, especially in crypto categories</p><p>• CVEs discovered in cryptographic implementations</p><p>• Experience with Docker, Git and writing automated tests</p><p>• Proficiency in C for low-level cryptographic work</p><p>Process</p><p>• Task vetting: complete a vetting task instead of a live interview</p><p>• Work is paid per task, with each task taking roughly 60-75 minutes</p><p>• Expected start around early November 2026</p>

<p>
  <strong>Headquarters:</strong> United States
    <br /><strong>URL:</strong> <a href="https://workforcenow.adp.com/mascsr/default/mdf/recruitment/recruitment.html?cid=fc2a6c7e-ef54-4ed9-8c04-d5aca23f99e3">https://workforcenow.adp.com/mascsr/default/mdf/recruitment/recruitment.html?cid=fc2a6c7e-ef54-4ed9-8c04-d5aca23f99e3</a>
</p>

<p><strong><span>Senior Software Engineer, eRx Enterprise and Gadget</span></strong></p><h1>About DrFirst</h1><p>For 25 years, DrFirst has empowered providers and patients to achieve better health through intelligent medication management. We improve healthcare workflows and help patients start and stay on therapy with end-to-end solutions that enhance prescription access, affordability, and adherence. Our solutions help 100 million patients a year and are used by more than 420,000 prescribers, 71,000 pharmacies, 270 EHRs and health information systems, and over 2,000 hospitals in the U.S. This is a great opportunity to be a part of a successful Healthcare IT company experiencing significant growth. Here you’ll get to work with some of the smartest and most interesting people around, solving unique and complex challenges in healthcare on a scale matched by few companies. If you get excited about stretching yourself in new ways, developing yourself to your fullest potential, and care about working with smart colleagues, we want to talk to you!</p><h1>Position Overview</h1><p>DrFirst is hiring a Senior Software Engineer for the eRx Enterprise and Gadget team. Your first focus is Gadget, our pharmacy agent. Over time you will extend your work into Rcopia, our ePrescribing platform, on Electronic Prescribing of Controlled Substances (EPCS) and Prescription Drug Monitoring Program (PDMP) workflows.</p><p>You will build cloud native, high performance services for an ePrescribing collaboration platform. The platform connects providers, patients, payers, pharmacies, and pharmaceutical companies in real time. You will design systems built for high load, with self healing, auto scaling, and full observability.</p><p>You bring strong judgment about AI. You know when AI speeds up delivery and when AI produces weak code. with reviewer feedback on submissions</p><p>• Expected start in early November 2026</p>

      <title>Custom Mechanical Solutions: Quality and Reliability Engineer</title>
      <region>USA Only</region>
      <category>Full-Stack Programming</category>
      <description>

<p>
  <strong>Headquarters:</strong> 
    <br /><strong>URL:</strong> <a href="http://cmswa.com">http://cmswa.com</a>
</p>

<div><p>Custom Mechanical Solutions delivers energy-efficient HVAC systems across the Pacific Northwest, with deep expertise in healthcare, education, data centers, and retrofit projects. We work with top manufacturers to meet performance and sustainability goals—always focused on quality, care, and progress.</p>
<p>If you're ready to grow your career, we’re glad you found us. At CMS, you’ll join a team that supports your development and gives you space to make an impact. &nbsp;We review every application carefully and appreciate your interest in growing your career with our team.</p></div><h2>About Custom Mechanical Solutions</h2>
<p>Custom Mechanical Solutions (CMS) provides commercial HVAC equipment and technical solutions for complex building applications. We partner with contractors, engineers, building owners, and manufacturers throughout the equipment lifecycle—from system design and delivery through startup, troubleshooting, and field support.</p>
<p>As part of the Meriton family of companies, CMS maintains its specialized technical expertise and customer-focused approach while benefiting from the resources and long-term investment of a growing national organization.</p>
<p><strong>Title:</strong> Quality &amp; Reliability Engineer<br><strong>Department:</strong> CMS National Accounts<br><strong>Location:</strong> Fully remote within the United States<br><strong>Travel:</strong> Approximately 10–20% domestic and international travel</p>
<p><strong>Turn field challenges into better products, stronger processes, and more reliable outcomes.</strong></p>
<p>Join a growing National Accounts team where your technical judgment, curiosity, and follow-through will connect the jobsite to the factory and help shape how quality is managed as the business scales.</p>
<h1>The opportunity</h1>
<p>CMS is looking for a Quality &amp; Reliability Engineer to own and continuously improve the field-to-factory quality feedback loop for custom commercial and industrial HVAC equipment. You will lead technical investigations, turn incomplete field information into clear problem statements, and keep root-cause and corrective-action work moving through verified closure.</p>
<p>This is a hands-on, highly collaborative role. You will work across field operations, project teams, customers, engineering, manufacturing, suppliers, and factory quality leaders. Your work will help teams respond faster, create repeatable repairs, reduce recurrence, and apply lessons learned to future projects.</p>
<p>Work from where you are. This is a fully remote position that can be based anywhere within the United States. Approximately 10-20% domestic and international travel is expected, including travel to customer sites and manufacturing facilities in Mexico. Travel may be heavier initially while you build relationships with key stakeholders and learn the factory systems. Travel to Mexico is generally expected up to four times per year to support investigations, gather technical evidence, collaborate with factory teams, and validate corrective actions.</p>
<h1>What you will own</h1>
<ul>
<li><strong>Lead field-to-factory investigations. </strong>Coordinate quality issues from initial report through containment, root cause, corrective action, and verified closure.</li>
<li><strong>Turn field intelligence into action. </strong>Gather the technical evidence needed for faster decisions and translate recurring trends into improvements in design, manufacturing, supplier controls, installation guidance, training, and documentation.</li>
<li><strong>Create field-ready solutions. </strong>Develop clear, controlled Field Service Bulletins with approved repair steps, safety requirements, acceptance criteria, and closeout evidence.</li>
<li><strong>Drive clarity and accountability. </strong>Keep owners, milestones, risks, decisions, and overdue actions visible. Remove blockers and escalate high-impact or aging issues when needed.</li>
<li><strong>Use data to improve the program. </strong>Maintain quality dashboards and reports, identify systemic trends and emerging risks, and provide concise updates to leadership, project teams, customers, and factory partners.</li>
<li><strong>Go where the evidence is. </strong>Travel to customer sites and manufacturing facilities in Mexico to inspect equipment, support troubleshooting, gather evidence, collaborate with factory teams, and validate repair effectiveness.</li>
</ul>
<h1>You will probably love this role if...</h1>
<ul>
<li>When something fails, your first question is “Why?” and you keep digging until the evidence supports the answer.</li>
<li>You enjoy both the technical details and the bigger picture, from walking a jobsite and troubleshooting equipment to explaining the path forward clearly.</li>
<li>You take ownership without waiting for every step to be laid out, bring the right people together, and keep work moving until the issue is truly closed.</li>
<li>You are comfortable influencing across teams, even when you do not directly manage the people involved.</li>
<li>You want to help build and improve a quality program, not simply maintain one.</li>
</ul>
<h1>Required qualifications</h1>
<ul>
<li>A bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Industrial, Manufacturing, or Quality Engineering, or an equivalent combination of technical education and relevant professional experience.</li>
<li>At least three years of relevant experience in manufacturing quality, field service, commissioning, reliability engineering, technical investigations, or related technical project support.</li>
<li>Strong mechanical and/or electrical investigation and troubleshooting skills.</li>
<li>Working knowledge of structured problem-solving methods such as RCA, CAPA, 8D, 5 Why, fishbone analysis, or FMEA. Ability to translate incomplete field information into clear technical problem statements and drive corrective actions through verified closure.</li>
<li>Ability to communicate complex technical issues clearly to technical and nontechnical audiences.</li>
<li>Ability to travel domestically and internationally approximately 10–20%, including travel to manufacturing facilities in Mexico.</li>
<li>A valid passport at the time of hire is preferred; candidates without one must be able to obtain one within the first 90 days of employment.</li>
</ul>
<h1>Preferred qualifications</h1>
<ul>
<li>Five or more years of relevant quality, reliability, field-service, commissioning, or technical investigation experience.</li>
<li>Direct experience with commercial or industrial HVAC equipment. Experience with custom air-handling equipment, controls, construction drawings and specifications, startup, commissioning, or active job-site processes.</li>
<li>Experience working directly with manufacturing facilities, suppliers, factory quality teams, or field-service organizations.</li>
<li>Experience developing technical repair procedures, Field Service Bulletins, corrective-action documentation, or quality dashboards.</li>
<li>Compensation and benefits Base salary: $95,000-$125,000 annually, depending on experience.</li>
<li>This position is also eligible for a discretionary bonus.</li>
<li>Eligible employees may participate in Meriton’s benefits programs in accordance with applicable plan terms.</li>
</ul>
<h1>Why CMS National Accounts</h1>
<p>You will join a fast-moving team supporting complex equipment and significant projects where expectations are high, and the connection between field performance and customer experience matters. This role offers the opportunity to make quality information more complete, corrective actions more durable, repairs more repeatable, and lessons learned more useful across a growing portfolio.</p>
<p><strong>If you are ready to solve meaningful technical problems and help build a stronger quality and reliability program, we would like to hear from you.</strong></p>
<p><strong>Custom Mechanical Solutions is an Equal Opportunity Employer</strong></p><div><p></p>
<p><span>Employment practices will not be influenced or affected by an applicant’s or employee’s race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy), national origin, age, disability, genetic information, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, veteran status or any other legally protected status. &nbsp;Reasonable accommodations will be made for qualified individuals with disabilities unless doing so would result in an undue hardship.</span></p>
<p><span>Salary ranges listed are dependent upon a candidate’s qualifications, experience, internal equity, and the budgeted amount for the specific role and location.</span></p></div>

</description>

      <region>Anywhere in the World</region>

      <description>

<p>
  <strong>Headquarters:</strong> Remote
</p>

<div class="content-intro"><p>Knock is redefining the home buying and selling experience, and we’re only getting started! We’re a passionate team of industry experts who knew there had to be a better, simpler way for people to navigate the journey between homes. That people-first mindset is core to how we operate, and why Knock has been honored as one of<em> Inc.’s Best Workplaces</em> six times in the past seven years.</p>
<p>We bring that mindset into the work we do every day.&nbsp; The Knock Bridge Loan™ empowers homebuyers to ‘buy before they sell’, by unlocking the equity in their current home, giving them greater convenience, certainty, and competitiveness.&nbsp;</p>
<p>Founded in 2015, Knock has grown into a trusted partner for thousands of homebuyers and a network of 60,000+ loan officers and agents across the country. Backed by top investors like Foundry Group, Trinity Capital, and the National Association of Realtors, we’ve built a reputation for innovation and trust, earning 900+ five-star Zillow and Trustpilot reviews and an A+ BBB rating.&nbsp;</p>
<p>Join our growing team and help shape the future of homebuying! To learn more, visit <a href="http://knock.com/">Knock.com</a></p></div><p><strong>Lending Manager (Front End)</strong></p>
<p><strong>About the role</strong></p>
<p><strong>Knock is looking for an experienced mortgage leader to manage and grow our team of fully remote Loan Assistants. This is a 100% remote role, and you’ll lead a team distributed across the country. You enjoy building teams, finding efficiencies, and using technology to improve how work gets done. You’re approachable, open-minded, and adaptable. You know the work well enough to coach it and you’re willing to jump in and help. In this role you’ll own the Loan Assistant and post-closing pipelines, develop your team, and work with the Director of Lending Operations to make our processes better.</strong></p>
<p><strong>What you’ll do:</strong></p>
<p><strong><em>Lead and develop the team</em></strong></p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Manage, lead, and scale the remote Loan Assistant team. </strong></li>
<li><strong>Share weekly, monthly, quarterly, and annual team and company goals, and make sure the team meets and exceeds expectations.Hold team members accountable for their performance.</strong></li>
<li><strong>Build camaraderie and teamwork in a virtual environment through team meetings and regular 1:1 check-ins.</strong></li>
<li><strong>Run virtual training for new Loan Assistants and serve as the team’s go-to for escalations, questions, and exceptions.</strong></li>
<li><strong>Mentor people inside and outside your team, and keep learning yourself.</strong></li>
<li><strong>Document conversations in our HRIS and build a sense of ownership across the team.</strong></li>
</ul>
<p><strong><em>Own the pipeline</em></strong></p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Manage the bridge loan pipeline from setup through initial disclosure and submission, and through post-closing. </strong></li>
<li><strong>Coach the team and give feedback along the way.Balance workloads across the team to meet company SLAs.</strong></li>
<li><strong>Support post-closing review. </strong></li>
<li><strong>Work loans that have findings with the team member responsible and get them resolved.</strong></li>
<li><strong>Work closely with Sales, Underwriting, and Closing to give everyone timely, accurate service.</strong></li>
<li><strong>Compile team scorecard data each quarter to track KPIs and quality.</strong></li>
</ul>
<p><strong><em>Improve how we work</em></strong></p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Help the Director of Lending Operations find gaps in process and policy across the Loan Assistant and post-closing functions. </strong></li>
<li><strong>Write or update procedures for review, training, and rollout, then follow up to make sure the changes stick.</strong></li>
<li><strong>Set best practices and change the workflow when needed so the team runs efficiently and meets company KPIs.</strong></li>
<li><strong>Take on ad hoc projects and step in wherever your team needs support.</strong></li>
