    ","descriptionBodyPlain":"Every dataset at Spotify, from the data behind creator royalties to the signals powering recommendations, is registered, published and traced through systems our team builds. We're the source of truth for what data exists at Spotify, where it lives, who owns it, and how it flows from one pipeline to the next. These systems sit on the critical path of the platform. Data teams use them every day to publish and find data, and other platform teams build on them for access, retention, governance and incident response. That means our work is judged on correctness and reliability, because every system built on top of ours is only as good as the metadata we provide. This is a backend role focused on data management, working on the problems at the core of any large data platform: running a data catalog that stays accurate at scale, capturing lineage across batch and streaming workloads, managing schemas as they evolve, and guaranteeing that consumers only read complete data. We build on open standards like OpenLineage and Apache Iceberg, and define the internal standards for naming, storage and metadata that the rest of Spotify builds against. As the platform takes on new storage technologies and new kinds of data assets, those standards and the systems behind them have to evolve with it, and you'll help decide how.   ","hostedUrl":"https://jobs.lever.co/spotify/186b763a-2a61-4563-8813-ff6b40c9c8a7","applyUrl":"https://jobs.lever.co/spotify/186b763a-2a61-4563-8813-ff6b40c9c8a7/apply"},{"additionalPlain":"Spotify is an equal opportunity employer.   • Shape and execute an integrated communications strategy for MENAT+, putting regional creators, audiences, and culture at the heart of Spotify’s storytelling.
  • Be a trusted communications partner to regional leadership, providing clear counsel on business priorities, reputation, emerging issues, and high-impact moments.
  • Anticipate reputational opportunities and risks and help Spotify respond thoughtfully and effectively as cultural, media, policy, and regulatory dynamics evolve.
  • Lead creator-first and earned-first storytelling that builds fandom, discovery, and cultural relevance, finding compelling stories in emerging scenes, communities, and moments that matter locally.
  • Partner with Music, Podcasts, Product, Growth, Marketing, Public Affairs, and other teams to develop communications that support Spotify’s regional priorities.
  • Connect MENAT+ priorities and perspectives with Spotify’s global communications strategy, while translating global priorities in ways that resonate with local audiences.
  • Lead corporate, executive, internal, and B2B communications, including executive positioning, thought leadership, media engagement, and strategic messaging.
  • Lead agency relationships and budgets with creativity and discipline, developing efficient approaches that deliver high-quality, locally relevant work across a diverse geographic footprint.

  • Email and nurture, moving people toward sales: Build nurture paths mapped to each stage from lead to opportunity with a clear next step. Keep lists clean and own subscription types and consent setup, including growing opted-in lists across the portfolio. Partner with Legal on consent, privacy and data sharing so every list enters HubSpot correctly and legally.

  • Reporting: Build reporting at campaign, channel and executive levels, and own the weekly scorecard. Track spend and tool costs against pipeline, decide with the team what to scale, fix or stop.

    Spotify is building the next generation of advertising, connecting brands with audiences through audio, video, and experiences that are deeply embedded in people's lives. As our advertising business evolves, demonstrating the impact of advertising on Spotify, and helping advertisers achieve better outcomes, will be critical to our long-term success.

    We are seeking a Head of Measurement & Advertising Effectiveness to define how Spotify proves the value of its advertising, advances measurement science, and makes advertiser effectiveness a lasting competitive advantage.

    Reporting directly to the SVP of Advertising, you will be a member of the global Advertising leadership team, operating within a business with end-to-end P&L accountability. You will play an influential role in shaping our strategy, guiding investment priorities, and strengthening the value we deliver to advertisers.

    This is an opportunity to build and lead a differentiated measurement and effectiveness organization at a time when the industry is being reshaped by AI, evolving privacy expectations, and increasing demand for measurable business outcomes. We are looking for a leader who combines scientific rigor, strategic vision, commercial judgment, and exceptional people leadership—and who can represent Spotify as a credible and influential voice in the industry.

  • Build and transform the function. Set Spotify’s global measurement and effectiveness vision across brand, performance, and full-funnel advertising, and fundamentally build and elevate our capabilities to get there.
  • Advance measurement science. Lead our approach to incrementality, causal inference, experimentation, attribution, marketing mix modeling, and brand lift, and set rigorous standards for how we measure advertiser outcomes.
  • Define what we need to prove. Set the scientific requirements for measuring advertising impact on Spotify, and influence investment priorities with Product, Engineering, and Data Science, who own building the solutions.
  • Turn evidence into advertiser growth. Build marketing science and consulting capabilities that help advertisers understand and improve their results on Spotify, and partner with commercial leaders to turn that evidence into deeper relationships and smarter investment decisions.
  • Tailor measurement by industry. Develop approaches that reflect the distinct goals and challenges of advertisers in key verticals.
  • Build research and partnerships. Set an ambitious research agenda, develop relationships with leading measurement and technology partners, and advance independent validation and new approaches.
  • Lead what’s next. Anticipate how AI, new methods, and ecosystem shifts will change measurement, and position Spotify to lead rather than follow.
  • Shape industry thinking. Go beyond representing Spotify to help shape how the industry approaches effectiveness and measurement standards, through direct engagement with CMOs and agency leaders, seats on industry boards, major conference stages, and thought leadership.
  • Build an exceptional organization. Design, scale, and lead a high-performing global team spanning measurement strategy, marketing science, advertiser consulting, research, and partnerships.
  • Shape Advertising leadership decisions. Bring scientific expertise, advertiser insight, and an evidence-based perspective to the leadership team’s strategic choices and long-term priorities.

  • Coordinate litigation, pre-litigation, regulatory, and other dispute matters across multiple practice areas, including copyright and patent litigation.
  • Work with outside counsel to develop case strategy, manage budgets, and drive efficient resolution of contentious disputes.
  • Partner with the business on litigation and legal risk issues and work with colleagues to fashion solutions that balance legal risk with company objectives.
  • Develop litigation case strategies, work closely with Spotify's communications team, and formulate plans to resolve disputes efficiently.
  • Plan strategically and coordinate internally with legal and non-legal personnel on issues of the moment.
  • Provide proactive advice to internal team members on dispute avoidance and resolution, including risk mitigation.
  • Identify and mitigate threats against the company, whether from partners, users, content owners, or others.
  • Handle requests for information from the company, including subpoenas and requests from law enforcement.
  • Build scalable processes to address a growing number of claims across copyright, patent, and other areas.
  • Train teams and draft workflows and policies to help establish effective internal risk mitigation procedures.
  • Stay current on developments in patent and copyright law, particularly as they affect the technology and media industries.

Join us and you’ll keep millions of users listening by making great recommendations to each and every one of them.

    At Spotify, great personalization is about more than recommending the right song. It's about creating listening experiences that feel effortless and meaningful while balancing the needs of listeners, creators, and our business.
    The Samba team, part of Spotify's Personalization Mission, works on multi-objective balancing and sequencing for personalized listening experiences like Autoplay, Radio, and Mixes.     We're looking for an Engineering Manager to lead this team, develop our engineers, and help shape the technical direction of systems that influence how millions of people experience Spotify.

    At Spotify, we’re building a thriving audiobook ecosystem that connects authors and publishers with listeners around the world.

    As our audiobook business expands into new markets, we’re looking for someone to grow our international publisher portfolio. You’ll build relationships with publishers of all sizes, help them bring their catalogues to Spotify, and shape scalable ways to onboard and support them. Your goal is to make Spotify a trusted home for publishers audiobooks, combining a welcoming partner experience with sustainable commercial growth.

    ","id":"358dac9a-7d46-432e-a1f3-2660cbe26591","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do","content":"
  • Identify and engage major and independent publishers across new markets, building a pipeline informed by local publishing landscapes, catalogue gaps, and listener demand.

  • Explain Spotify’s audiobook offering and guide publishers towards the right onboarding route, including Spotify for Authors sign-up and coordinated follow-up for large-catalogue enquiries.

  • Lead commercial and licensing negotiations where bespoke agreements are needed, managing distribution terms, licensing budgets, and deal structures that balance partner value, cost, and long-term growth.

  • Work with publishers and operations on catalogue readiness, metadata, and content delivery in coordination with the operational team, resolving barriers from initial interest through to titles going live.

  • Develop scalable onboarding processes, guidance, and communications with product and operations teams, making it easier for publishers of all sizes to get started and stay supported.

  • Own long-term publisher relationships, tailoring communications, shared goals, and performance reviews to the needs of a growing and diverse partner base.

  • Represent publishers internally, translating their feedback into improvements with product, editorial, growth, operations, and cost management teams.

  • Track pipeline conversion, onboarding completion, catalogue growth, and partner feedback to identify bottlenecks, prioritise opportunities, and improve the publisher experience.

    • "},{"text":"Who You Are","content":"

  • You have experience in licensing, partnerships, business affairs, or business development in digital content, with a track record of negotiating and managing agreements with rights holders.

  • You have experience growing partner portfolios or developing onboarding and engagement programmes that serve a broad partner base.

  • Knowledge of international publishing and audiobook ecosystems, including distribution models, and an established publisher network are advantages.

  • You’re comfortable assessing catalogues, interpreting performance data and financial models, and managing budgets to balance partner value, cost, and growth.

  • You take ownership, collaborate effectively across teams, and stay organised while managing multiple markets and priorities in a fast-moving environment.

  • You have full professional proficiency in English. Additional languages relevant to our international markets are an advantage.

    Conduct groundbreaking research in generative audio using diffusion or flow matching models, with a focus on one or more of the following areas:
     
    Vocal Synthesis — Research in vocal and speech synthesis, along with related areas such as ML-based audio processing and signal processing.
     
    Post-Training — Research in post-training techniques for music generation, including preference alignment methods (such as DPO, RLHF, or KTO), reward model design and training, and reinforcement learning to improve output quality, controllability, and human preference adherence.
     
    Editing — Research in iterative music generation and audio editing, including capabilities such as stem replacement, instrumentation change, mood changes (while preserving content), tempo changes, and structure changes.
     
    You will also:
  • Run large-scale experiments with access to Spotify's extensive infrastructure and an audience of more than 700 million monthly active users.
  • Create practical applications that harness generative technologies and push the boundaries of what's possible in listening experiences.
  • Collaborate as part of a cross-functional team—working closely with scientists, engineers, product managers, designers, user researchers, and analysts—to craft innovative solutions to complex challenges.
  • Have a direct impact on Spotify's products, tools, and services, working on projects that influence the entire organization.
  • Engage with the broader research community by publishing your findings, delivering talks, and attending top conferences.

    At Spotify, our mission is to unlock the potential of human creativity by connecting creators with fans and helping listeners discover the audio they love. As we continue to grow in India, building lasting relationships with our listeners is central to our success.

    Our Marketing team plays a key role in shaping how people discover, experience and stay connected to Spotify. We're looking for a Retention & Engagement Marketing Lead to develop strategies that deepen listener engagement, reduce churn and bring inactive users back. You'll combine consumer insights, data and creativity to build experiences that give listeners more reasons to return to Spotify.

    ","id":"9057bb9b-3aa2-49ba-9fd0-a9395018d0ea","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do","content":"

  • Lead Spotify India's consumer retention and engagement marketing strategy across the listener lifecycle, from new and active users to dormant and lapsed listeners.

  • Identify the key drivers of disengagement and churn, and develop targeted strategies that encourage repeat listening and long-term retention.

  • Build tailored retention and re-engagement strategies for different listener segments, using behavioural insights, preferences and engagement patterns.

  • Create personalised listener journeys that connect audiences with relevant music, artists, content and Spotify features.

  • Partner with Data Science, Analytics and Consumer Insights teams to uncover engagement opportunities and turn consumer insights into actionable marketing initiatives.

  • Define and track key performance indicators, including retention, churn, reactivation, daily and monthly active users, and engagement. Use experimentation to measure incremental impact and continuously improve results.

  • Collaborate with Product, Music, Brand, Media and Consumer Marketing teams to develop a connected retention roadmap that brings together product experiences, music releases, artists and cultural moments.

  • Translate insights and performance trends into clear recommendations that influence marketing priorities and drive measurable business outcomes.

    • "},{"text":"Who You Are","content":"

  • You have 8+ years of experience in growth, lifecycle, retention or customer relationship management (CRM) marketing, with a track record of driving consumer engagement and retention.

  • You understand consumer behaviour and know how to turn insights into strategies that encourage repeat usage and build long-term relationships.

  • You have experience developing segmentation strategies, personalised consumer journeys and engagement programmes for large consumer audiences.

  • You are confident working with data, analytics and experimentation to identify opportunities, evaluate performance and make informed decisions.

  • You think beyond individual campaigns and channels, focusing on how marketing can influence consumer behaviour and deliver measurable business impact.

  • You can bring teams together around shared goals and collaborate effectively with Product, Analytics, Data Science and Marketing partners.

  • You are comfortable balancing long-term strategy with hands-on execution, adapting your approach as you learn what works.

  • You are curious about music, culture and how digital experiences can create meaningful connections with listeners.

    As Revenue Operations Manager, you'll own revenue operations for Spotify Technology, helping our sales organization scale from early growth to a mature, segmented go-to-market model. This is a hands-on role where you'll work closely with the business day to day, identify challenges early, and build the systems, processes, and insights that enable sustainable growth.

    ","id":"66184cac-4d6c-46f6-868c-bac0c184fd22","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do","content":"

    • Own sales operations for Spotify Technology, including CRM, pipeline management, forecasting, territory and account assignment, and deal desk processes.

    • Design and roll out a segmented sales model that evolves our go-to-market approach as the business matures.

    • Build infrastructure and systems to support a scalable Commercial sales motion (companies with fewer than 1,000 employees), focused on faster deal cycles, efficient lead routing, and repeatable processes.

    • Build infrastructure and systems to support a strategic Enterprise sales motion (companies with 1,000+ employees), enabling prospecting, account planning, and multi-product engagements.

    • Partner with the Director of Sales as a strategic advisor on quota setting, capacity planning, compensation, territory design, and headcount modeling.

    • Support revenue across the full customer lifecycle, including new business, expansion, and retention.

    • Build reporting and dashboards to track pipeline coverage, conversion rates, time to close, forecast accuracy, and net revenue retention by segment.

    • Strengthen forecasting discipline and maintain a healthy, predictable pipeline through effective reporting and sales processes.

    • Identify friction across the sales process, including handoffs between Account Executives, Sales Engineering, and Customer Success, and drive improvements with cross-functional partners.

    • Partner with Marketing on pipeline generation reporting, lead management, and process improvements.

    • Establish and continuously improve operating rhythms, including forecast calls, pipeline reviews, and quarterly business reviews (QBRs), as the business scales.

    • Evaluate and manage the go-to-market (GTM) technology stack to support efficient and scalable sales operations.

    "},{"text":"Who You Are","content":"

    • You have 6+ years of experience in revenue operations, sales operations, or go-to-market strategy, with a track record of meaningful impact at a senior level.

    • You have experience scaling sales operations through a startup or high-growth phase and understand when to introduce new processes and structure.

    • You can build systems and processes from the ground up without adding unnecessary complexity.

    • You are proficient in using AI and can lead initiatives that improve sales effectiveness through AI-enabled tools and processes.

    • You have experience in B2B SaaS, ideally within developer platforms, DevOps tools, or cloud services.

    • You understand the differences between product-led growth (PLG), Commercial, and Enterprise sales motions and have experience designing segmented sales models.

    • You understand complex technical sales involving Sales Engineering and recognize the importance of customer retention and post-sale success in revenue strategy.

    • You have hands-on experience with Salesforce or a similar CRM, including building reports, workflows, and resolving data issues.

    • You use data to guide forecasting, capacity modeling, and funnel analysis, combining analytical skills with sound business judgment.

    • You can influence senior sales leaders, build alignment across teams, and drive decisions without formal authority.

    • You are comfortable working in evolving environments, adapting as priorities change, and helping shape how an innovative business grows.

    • Lead, coach, and develop a team of Enterprise Account Executives, helping each seller grow their skills and consistently achieve or exceed their targets.

    • Own quarterly and annual team revenue targets for new business with organizations of 1,000+ employees, in partnership with the Director of Sales.

    • Translate Spotify Technology's overall sales strategy into a clear enterprise plan, including target accounts, territory priorities, and account planning standards.

    • Build a team that converts inbound demand while proactively hunting new opportunities in target accounts.

    • Stay hands-on in key deals, joining customer meetings, supporting negotiations, and helping navigate complex buying committees.

    • Coach the team on strategic account planning, multi-threading, champion building, and developing executive-level business cases.

    • Run a disciplined operating rhythm through regular pipeline reviews, deal reviews, and one-on-ones, while maintaining accurate forecasts and a healthy, predictable pipeline for long-cycle deals.

    • Partner with Revenue Operations on territory design, reporting, and process improvements for the Enterprise segment.

    • Collaborate with Sales Engineering on technical evaluations and proofs of concept, with Customer Success on retention and expansion, and with Marketing on account-based programs and pipeline generation.

    • Help sellers articulate how Backstage Portal, Confidence, and Xirp solve developer experience challenges, including how AI is reshaping software development in large organizations.

    • Help sellers tell a compelling story about Spotify's internal approach to solving engineering challenges and how our products are proven internally at scale.

    • Share customer feedback with Product and internal teams to help shape the roadmap.

    • Contribute to hiring, onboarding, and developing sales playbooks as the Enterprise team grows.

    "},{"text":"Who You Are","content":"

    • You are both strategic and hands-on, comfortable setting direction while staying involved in the details of individual deals.

    • You bring strong judgment when working with incomplete information and can coach your team to prioritize high-potential opportunities while confidently moving away from poorly qualified deals.

    • You have experience selling to engineering leaders, CTOs, platform teams, or developer experience buyers, and understand how they evaluate and make purchasing decisions.

    • You are familiar with software development, Product Management, DevOps tools, or developer ecosystems.

    • You understand long, multi-stakeholder sales cycles, including procurement processes, security reviews, and multi-year agreements.

    • You have experience partnering closely with Sales Engineering and understand the importance of technical depth in complex enterprise sales.

    • You use data and metrics to guide forecasting, coaching, and decision-making, while building structure and processes without adding unnecessary complexity.

    • You bring strong communication, coaching, negotiation, and presentation skills.

    • You are excited to help build a scalable enterprise sales motion with AI and enjoy working with innovative products in an evolving technology landscape.

    Security engineers at Spotify help protect our environment and more than 700 million users. Within Platform, our Product Security team evaluates and communicates Spotify's security posture, helping developers and leadership make informed decisions about security risks. We own the vulnerability management platform, supporting the full lifecycle of identifying, attributing, remediating, and reporting security vulnerabilities.

    As AI changes how vulnerabilities are discovered and exploited, we're evolving how Spotify responds. We're looking for a Security Engineer to help transform vulnerability findings into reliable, actionable code improvements using agentic AI. You'll build the tools, workflows, and evaluation frameworks that make automated remediation more effective, scalable, and safe, while helping developers focus on building great experiences for our users.

  • Build and improve agentic AI workflows that turn security vulnerability findings into tested, review-ready code changes for engineering teams across Spotify.

  • Design and implement evaluation frameworks to measure the quality of automated fixes, including correctness, completeness, safety, build and test success, and pull request merge rates.

  • Develop tools and processes to compare remediation approaches, evaluate AI models, and continuously improve the reliability and effectiveness of generated fixes.

  • Research and apply emerging practices in AI-assisted vulnerability remediation, including prompt engineering, context engineering, and vulnerability-specific fix guidance.

  • Identify which vulnerability types are suitable for automated remediation, balancing security impact, technical feasibility, and developer experience.

  • Collaborate with developers and security stakeholders to collect feedback through code reviews, pull requests, support channels, and interactive sessions, using these insights to improve remediation quality.

  • Help shape how Spotify approaches security posture management by building scalable solutions that reduce security risks and make it easier for teams to address vulnerabilities.

  • You have worked with agentic AI systems or AI-assisted development workflows and understand how to apply them to real-world engineering challenges.

  • You are familiar with agentic AI frameworks and approaches to evaluating the quality, reliability, and safety of AI-generated outputs.

  • You enjoy collaborating across teams, learning from feedback, and navigating ambiguity. You're comfortable experimenting with new approaches while balancing innovation with thoughtful security decisions.

    We’re looking for a Senior C++/iOS Engineer to join the Baldur squad within User Platform (UP). Baldur owns Spotify’s Session Management and Delegated Authorization domains—the systems that enable applications to securely obtain, use, and manage access tokens for hundreds of millions of users. In this role, you’ll help shape the technology that powers secure access across every Spotify client and third-party integration. 

    Your work will support engineers across Spotify building mobile and desktop experiences, platform teams, and third-party developers integrating with Spotify’s authorization platform. You’ll collaborate across disciplines to build secure, reliable, and scalable authentication experiences that have a direct impact on millions of people every day.

  • Design, build, and evolve critical infrastructure powering Spotify applications and partner integrations using shared C++ libraries and native Swift on iOS.
  • Develop secure, reliable, and performant delegated authorization flows, including token issuance, refresh, revocation, and session lifecycle management across multiple platforms.
  • Partner with client and backend engineers to integrate with core authorization services, token issuance, client registration, and token revocation.
  • Improve how credentials and access tokens are securely stored and managed on-device while balancing security, reliability, and application performance.
  • Contribute to the evolution of Spotify’s authorization frameworks, Spotify-specific implementations, enabling new platforms and product experiences.
  • Drive technical improvements, share knowledge with teammates, and help shape the long-term technical direction of delegated authorization and session management.

    The Music Mission team owns Spotify's end to end proposition for music creators and the experiences they create for fans. The team is dedicated to building tools and services to enable creation, promotion, expression, and monetization at scale.

    We're looking for a Senior Data Scientist to join the Artist-First AI Music lab. Our team explores and advances generative technologies for music to create new experiences for fans and artists, with a focus on listening experiences that center and celebrate artists and creatives. All of our products will put artists and songwriters first, through these four principles:

    Partnerships with record labels, distributors, and music publishers: We'll develop new products for artists and fans through upfront agreements, not by asking for forgiveness later.

    Choice in participation: We recognize there's a wide range of views on use of generative music tools within the artistic community. Therefore, artists and rightsholders will choose if and how to participate to ensure the use of AI tools aligns with the values of the people behind the music.

    Fair compensation and new revenue: We will build products that create wholly new revenue streams for rightsholders, artists, and songwriters, ensuring they are properly compensated for uses of their work and transparently credited for their contributions.

    Artist-fan connection: AI tools we develop will not replace human artistry. They will give artists new ways to be creative and connect with fans. We will use our role as the place where more than 700 million people already come to listen to music every month to ensure that generative AI deepens artist-fan connections.

    For more information, see this press release: https://newsroom.spotify.com/2025-10-16/artist-first-ai-music-spotify-collaboration/

    ","id":"babebec3-0061-4c39-a4ad-c51a54d23567","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do","content":"
  • Lead foundational measurement and insights work for generative music experiences, developing the frameworks that help Spotify understand how creators, listeners, and rights holders engage with generative AI music.
  • Design and run large-scale analyses and evaluations of generative music systems, from prompt interpretation to model output quality, using Spotify's unique behavioral datasets, annotations, and experimentation platforms.
  • Partner with Engineers and AI Researchers to integrate evaluation signals into model development loops, debugging workflows, and product iteration, making sure scientific rigor informs technical direction.
  • Identify the behavioral and market dynamics that shape sustainable consumer demand and creator participation, and translate them into clear strategic recommendations.
  • Build practical, scalable metrics and decision systems that define what "good" looks like for AI music: credibility, user delight, safety, creator alignment, and ecosystem trust.
  • Bring together model, user behavior, and ecosystem signals into clear narratives that shape product strategy, cross-functional alignment, and long-term priorities across Spotify.
  • Create the datasets, dashboards, and long-term measurement systems that give Spotify a lasting, comprehensive understanding of product health and impact.
  • Work closely with Product, Design, Research, Legal, Trust & Safety, Marketing, Policy, and Licensing teams, bringing statistical rigor and principled measurement to help build artist-first systems that scale responsibly.
    • "},{"text":"Who You Are ","content":"
  • You have a track record of using insights to shape strategy for major company initiatives involving many different partners.
  • You have significant hands-on experience in advanced analytics or data science, ideally in a domain involving LLM evaluation, user-generated content, or complex user behavior.
  • You communicate clearly, form well-founded, evidence-backed points of view, and can bring together messy, multimodal signals (quantitative, qualitative, and model telemetry) into clear narratives for senior executives, researchers, engineers, and the music industry.
  • You're proficient in advanced analytics with Python and SQL, have analyzed large datasets, and use AI tools (e.g. Cursor, Copilot) to increase your productivity and impact.
  • You have experience developing metrics frameworks for complex products that help teams measure impact and reason clearly about priorities.
  • You have experience with machine learning frameworks, designing and assessing multimodal or embedding-based models, and validating them against LLM judges or human ground truth, with an understanding of how to evaluate models beyond offline accuracy.
  • You have a solid grounding in experimental design and causal inference, such as A/B tests, quasi-experiments, and power analysis.
  • You thrive when tackling loosely defined problems in ambiguous, zero-to-one spaces.
    • "},{"text":"Where You'll Be ","content":"

  • Manage multiple learning projects from initial scoping through delivery while creating clarity around priorities, timelines, and stakeholder expectations.

    Spotify is shaping the future of advertising by connecting brands with fans through audio, video, and experiences that are part of people's everyday lives. As our advertising business grows, we're focused on bringing innovative products to market, helping advertisers succeed, and turning new ideas into meaningful business growth.

    We're looking for a Senior Director, Global Advertising Product Marketing to lead the next chapter of our global Advertising Product Marketing team. Reporting to the Head of Advertising Business Marketing, you'll work closely with Product, Engineering, Sales, Business Development, and Marketing leaders to shape product strategy, strengthen our market position, and help advertisers get more value from Spotify.

    This is an opportunity to build and lead a product marketing function with a clear voice in product decisions and a direct impact on business growth. You'll bring customer insights into product development, establish a disciplined approach to go-to-market execution and product adoption, create compelling reasons for advertisers to choose Spotify, and help a global team deliver measurable results.

    ","id":"b9533f31-7bff-43f6-aaf0-60003f017d88","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do","content":"
  • Set the vision, strategy, and operating model for global Advertising Product Marketing, connecting advertiser needs, product innovation, competitive insights, and business growth.
  • Partner with Product, Engineering, Sales, Business Development, and Marketing leaders to bring customer and market insights into product decisions and turn innovation into solutions advertisers value.
  • Lead global go-to-market strategies for Spotify's advertising products, including brand and performance advertising, self-service, programmatic, and emerging solutions. Own product positioning, messaging, packaging, launches, and adoption.
  • Build a deeper understanding of advertisers, agencies, buying behaviors, and the competitive landscape. Use these insights to identify opportunities, influence product priorities, and strengthen Spotify's position in the market.
  • Drive product adoption and commercial growth by identifying customer needs, addressing barriers to adoption, and partnering with teams to improve product usage, retention, and revenue. Define clear measures of success and use results to guide future decisions.
  • Turn complex advertising technology, data, and measurement capabilities into clear, differentiated customer value propositions tied to measurable business outcomes. Partner with Business Marketing to create a consistent story across products and help advertisers understand the impact Spotify can deliver.
  • Strengthen how products move from development to market. Establish clear processes, shared accountability, and measures of readiness that help teams make informed decisions about when to launch, scale, improve, or stop initiatives.
  • Equip Sales and regional teams with the insights, messaging, and tools they need to bring Spotify's advertising solutions to customers. 
  • Work with Measurement and Advertising Effectiveness teams to connect product capabilities with credible evidence of advertiser outcomes, and feed that evidence back into product decisions
  • Explore how AI, automation, and emerging advertising technologies can improve our products, customer experiences, and product marketing practices and identify opportunities to rethink how Spotify develops, positions, and scales its advertising solutions.
  • Lead and develop a high-performing global Product Marketing organization, attracting outstanding talent, strengthening strategic and commercial capabilities, and creating a culture of creativity, accountability, collaboration, and measurable impact.

    The Policy & Safety team sits within Content Platform in the Experience Mission, building the systems that keep Spotify safe, compliant, and trusted by millions of users and creators. This team owns Spotify’s content moderation infrastructure — from detection models to policy enforcement systems and compliance data pipelines.

    Working at the intersection of machine learning, platform engineering, and regulatory compliance, the team partners closely with Trust & Safety, Legal, and Public Affairs. They’re on the critical path for every new content type and social feature — including messaging, comments, and collaborative experiences — ensuring safety is built in from day one.     The Platform team creates the technology that enables Spotify to learn quickly and scale easily, enabling rapid growth in our users and our business around the globe. Spanning many disciplines, we work to make the business work; creating the infrastructure, tooling, frameworks, and capabilities needed to welcome a billion customers.

    Spotify is looking for a Senior Software Engineer to join the Authorization team within Platform. Our team builds and operates the authorization and permissioning systems that enable creators and their teams to securely access and manage their presence across Spotify. What began by supporting Spotify for Artists has grown into foundational capabilities used across Spotify, including Music, Podcasts, and Audiobooks.

    This is a backend-focused role working on systems that sit on a critical path for Spotify's creator ecosystem. You'll help us evolve these systems as they grow in scale and complexity, bringing strong backend engineering expertise while collaborating across product, frontend, and data when needed.

    ","id":"e04833c0-9cff-4b5e-b217-91a3bcb57051","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do:","content":"

  • Design, build, deploy, and operate scalable backend services that power authorization, permissions, and team management across Spotify.

  • Take ownership of critical systems that enable creators, teams, agents, licensors, and other partners to securely access and manage the right content and capabilities.

  • Evolve our backend architecture to support continued growth in users, use cases, and Spotify products while maintaining high standards for reliability, performance, and security.

  • Improve the systems and workflows that enable creators to gain access to their content, profiles, and teams.

  • Make thoughtful technical decisions and trade-offs, balancing long-term architecture with solutions that meet current product and business needs.

  • Partner with engineers and cross-functional collaborators across Spotify to understand authorization needs and build reusable platform capabilities.

  • Contribute to frontend experiences and data-related work when useful, while bringing deep expertise and leadership to backend engineering.

  • Raise engineering quality through strong technical judgment, design discussions, operational excellence, and knowledge sharing across the team.

  • Run each studio project from brief to wrap, covering scope, timeline and run-of-show, in partnership with an Audio Engineer and the wider ALP team
  • Manage project budgets for studio support, photographers, licensing and freelancers, and make sure agreements with artists, labels and vendors are in place with a fair value exchange
  • Adapt global video initiatives and formats for Sweden and the Nordics, track results, and evolve the program to fit market needs
  • Partner with Marketing and Growth to promote studio content on the Spotify platform through in-app placements such as banners and Marquee-style campaigns
  • Project manage selected ALP initiatives, such as live events, marketing campaigns and superfan activations, from planning to delivery

    We’re looking for a Tax Manager to join Spotify’s Global Transfer Pricing team, reporting to the Director of Global Transfer Pricing. In this role you’ll focus on analytics, modelling and AI. You’ll drive the development of Spotify’s global transfer pricing models and economic analyses, keeping our intercompany pricing accurate, efficient and defensible in every jurisdiction where we operate. You’ll also help lead the team’s use of AI tools and automation to change how transfer pricing work gets done, from forecasting and projections to audit support. You’ll join a team of skilled, dedicated colleagues in a fast-moving international company, with plenty of room to take on responsibility. Above all, your work will impact the way the world experiences audio.
    ","id":"3a0d23b5-5dda-456a-967b-0fcada78daf1","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do","content":"
  • Develop, maintain and continuously improve Spotify’s global transfer pricing models for quarter-end and year-end closes.
  • Prepare and review quarterly and annual transfer pricing calculations, delivering them within internal and reporting deadlines.
  • Turn externally prepared benchmarking studies and economic analyses into practical inputs for our transfer pricing models.
  • Partner with FP&A and finance business partners on future transfer pricing outcomes and projections.
  • Drive the adoption of AI tools and automation to make transfer pricing processes more efficient, accurate and scalable.
  • Work with Spotify’s data and technology teams to transform how financial data for transfer pricing transactions is sourced and handled.
  • Collaborate with Tax, Treasury, Accounting and Legal on transfer pricing matters, and support tax audits with documentation, analyses and outcome scenarios.

  • Set the engineering strategy and architecture.   • Scale our advertising technology. Lead engineering across Ads Manager, Spotify Ad Exchange, ad serving, programmatic integrations, data infrastructure, and machine learning-based optimization.

  • Raise the bar on platform reliability. Advance standards across availability, latency, delivery accuracy, data quality, observability, incident management, and production resilience.

  • Advance intelligent advertising. Develop capabilities across real-time decisioning, auctions, bidding, targeting, relevance, pacing, pricing, and optimization to improve advertiser outcomes, monetization, and listener experience.

  • Partner across the Advertising leadership team. Work closely with Product, Data Science, and Commercial leadership to connect technical investments to customer value and business growth. Bring engineering perspective to major business decisions.

  • Build and develop the engineering organization. Attract exceptional technical leaders, strengthen succession, and foster a culture of ownership, accountability, and continuous improvement.

Tech.eu https://tech.eu en Mon, 23 Nov 2026 14:53:00 +0000 hourly 1 <![CDATA[Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO following “input” from US government]]> https://tech.eu/2026/11/23/jensen-huang-reinstated-as-nvidia-ceo-following-input-from-us-government/ https://tech.eu/2026/11/23/jensen-huang-reinstated-as-nvidia-ceo-following-input-from-us-government/#comments Jensen Huang has been reinstated as CEO and president of Nvidia, the Nvidia board announced today, in a shock announcement.

The Nvidia board said it had voted unanimously to reinstate Huang, who resigned earlier this month, following reports of extramarital affairs, including with a businesswoman US authorities suspected of spying for China.

Huang admitted he had an affair with the woman who was allleged to be a Chinese spy.

Huang, the Nvidia co-founder, is synonymous with Nvidia, which is the US tech firm powering much of the AI revolution. Hs is returning as leader wiith immediate effect, the board said.

Nvidia said its decision to reinstate Huang came after “input from senior levels of the United States government".

The decision follows President Donald Trump on Sunday night posting on social media: “I hope the Board of Nvidia rehires Jensen Huang. It would be the best thing for the Company, and also, for the USA."

In a statement, the board said: “The Board of Directors voted unanimously to reinstate Mr Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr Huang’s candor and ability to lead Nvidia.

"In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk."

“The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” said Harvey C. Jones, Chair of the Board.

“We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company. We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as Nvidia's Chief Financial Officer.” 

President Trump endorsed the decision, saying the board had "made the correct and proper decision".

Image: ChatGPT

]]> https://tech.eu/2026/11/23/jensen-huang-reinstated-as-nvidia-ceo-following-input-from-us-government/ Mon, 23 Nov 2026 14:53:00 +0000 https://tech.eu/2026/11/23/jensen-huang-reinstated-as-nvidia-ceo-following-input-from-us-government/feed 0 false <![CDATA[BBB invests £43M in Oxford University spinout backer]]> https://tech.eu/2026/11/23/bbb-invests-ps43m-in-oxford-university-spinout-backer/ https://tech.eu/2026/11/23/bbb-invests-ps43m-in-oxford-university-spinout-backer/#comments The British Business Bank (BBB) has acquired a £43m stake in Oxford Science Enterprises (OSE), an independent venture company that helps turn University of Oxford research into startups.

The £43m investment marks the BBB’s first investment in OSE, as it looks to scale the UK’s university spinout ecosystem.

The UK state-owned BBB and OSE have previously co-invested in ten Oxford University spinouts, most recently AI chip startup Fractile, with OSE the first investor in Fractile. They have also co-invested in OMass Therapeutics, Quantum Motion, and Oxford Quantum Circuits.

European spinouts have raised $13.8bn so far in 2026, with OSE’s portfolio contributing $1.5bn in the first nine months.

The BBB said the partnership between the BBB and the OBE will deepen collaboration on future co-investments and give OSE’s portfolio companies greater access to the BBB’s long-term capital as they scale.

OSE, founded in 2015, is an independent investment company, which aims to turn University of Oxford research into startups. It works with academics to form companies and invests in areas including life sciences, healthtech and deeptech. The University of Oxford owns five per cent of OSE.

OSE has had two major exits behind it: quantum computing company Oxford Ionics was acquired by US-listed IonQ for $1.075bn last year and biotech firm Dark Blue Therapeutics was acquired by Amgen in a $840m deaf completed last year.

Leandros Kalisperas, Chief Investment Officer, the British Business Bank, said: “By working more closely with OSE, we aim to help high-potential spinouts to grow faster and ensure the UK benefits from the breakthroughs it creates.”

Ed Bussey, CEO of Oxford Science Enterprises, said: “OSE is emerging as the world’s largest venture builder of deep science companies dedicated to a single university – a flagship in an area in which the UK now leads the world, at a time of unparalleled need for stronger economic growth and national resilience.

“This investment is a hugely welcome endorsement of the strategic importance of OSE to the UK’s future prosperity, health and security and I’m looking forward to working closely with the British Business Bank to meaningfully improve all of these outcomes to the benefit of the whole of the UK.”

]]> https://tech.eu/2026/11/23/bbb-invests-ps43m-in-oxford-university-spinout-backer/ Mon, 23 Nov 2026 11:53:00 +0000 https://tech.eu/2026/11/23/bbb-invests-ps43m-in-oxford-university-spinout-backer/feed 0 false <![CDATA[Defence startup Agon raises $70M, with UK's SovAI and NSSIF investing]]> https://tech.eu/2026/11/23/defence-startup-agon-raises-70m-with-uk-sovai-and-nssif-investing/ https://tech.eu/2026/11/23/defence-startup-agon-raises-70m-with-uk-sovai-and-nssif-investing/#comments A British defence startup founded by a former Anduril director, which is building virtual battlefields where AI-powered autonomous weapons practice fighting, has raised $70m in a Series A fuding round, less than six months after its $30m seed funding round.

Agon's new funding round was led by existing investor Northzone, along with other existing investors, including Lakestar, XYZ, Lux Capital, Global Founders Capital, and Speedinvest.

The UK Sovereign AI Fund, the UK government's VC fund established to scale up UK AI startups, and the National Security Strategic Investment Fund (NSSIF), the UK government's deeptech venture capital fund for national security and defence, have invested together for the first time, Agon said.

Roelof Botha, who led Sequoia between 2022 and 2025, has also invested.

The latest funding round values Agon at $450m and Agon says it marks one of the largest European defence technology Series A rounds of 2026. In total, it has now raised around $100m.

Founded in 2026, Agon is pitching itself as a startup that builds the infrastructure that designs, trains and iterates AI systems faster than adversaries.  Its tech provides its customers with AI training data to help in combat. The startup is making a play about its sovereign credentials, saying that Europe needs the sovereign capability to train and evolve AI.

It says it has signed initial partnerships with European defence companies and government customers. Its “synthetic” battlefield is aimed at helping its customers train their weapons to repel enemies, so for instance, using AI technology, counterdrone weapons can practice downing drone swarms or test how autonomous systems operate when communications are disrupted, navigation is degraded or adversary tactics change.

It claims that its technology gives defence companies, AI developers and governments the best chance of success on the battlefield.

UK-founded Agon, which has offices in London and Berlin, was founded by former soldier and former Anduril director Tristam Constant and Junaid Hussain, who is the co-founder of another British defence startup, Cambridge Aerospace and Google-backed AI and gaming company Iconic.

The new funding will be used to build its engineering and research teams, speed up the development of its platform, and expand its work with its clients.

Constant, co-founder and CEO of Agon, said: "Europe is in an AI arms race as we enter the era of agentic warfare: intelligent agents and machines that will need to understand their environment, make decisions and adapt at a speed and scale that humans alone cannot match.   

"We exist to build the sovereign infrastructure and AI foundation models to allow us to train, test, and evolve autonomous defence systems – in Europe, for Europe – to outperform adversary capabilities.

“Agon was born out of a project to bring together a coalition of European founders, operators, researchers, veterans, investors, and governments to build what we collectively believe to be urgently needed for our sovereignty and safety.”

]]> https://tech.eu/2026/11/23/defence-startup-agon-raises-70m-with-uk-sovai-and-nssif-investing/ Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:24:00 +0000 https://tech.eu/2026/11/23/defence-startup-agon-raises-70m-with-uk-sovai-and-nssif-investing/feed 0 false <![CDATA[Swiss startup coprod raises $6M to make building robot hardware as simple as developing software]]> https://tech.eu/2026/11/23/swiss-startup-coprod-raises-6m-to-make-building-robot-hardware-as-simple-as-developing-software/ https://tech.eu/2026/11/23/swiss-startup-coprod-raises-6m-to-make-building-robot-hardware-as-simple-as-developing-software/#comments Robotics hardware startup coprod has raised $6 million in a pre-seed funding round led by Founderful and PROTOTYPE, with participation from General Catalyst, Pace Ventures, Tiny Supercomputer Investment Company, Kima Ventures, SDAC, Unruly Capital and Venturekick. The round also attracted angel investors, including Hugging Face founder Thomas Wolf, the Dassault family and Florent Perrichon.

Founded in late 2024 by graduates of the École polytechnique fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL), coprod develops compatible hardware components for robotics and physical AI applications, aiming to reduce the time, cost and complexity of building specialised robotic systems.

Developing robots with custom hardware typically requires significant investment, specialised engineering teams and several years of development. One of the main challenges is integrating components from different suppliers, which often use incompatible systems and require extensive custom electronics and software work.

coprod aims to simplify this process through an ecosystem of compatible hardware components, called "co:products", supported by a software API and configuration tool. The platform standardises communication between components while maintaining the real-time performance needed for reliable robotic systems.

According to the company, its approach could reduce development timelines from two to three years to a few months, allowing smaller teams to build and test robotic platforms at an estimated cost of $5,000 to $25,000 per design iteration.

The founders initially demonstrated their approach by building a bipedal robot in a garage in the Swiss Alps. Since then, coprod's components have been integrated into several robotic projects in Switzerland, including the first student-built Swiss humanoid robot developed by the ETH Robotics Club, which recently took its first steps in Zurich.

Loïc Delineau, CEO and co-founder of coprod, said that simplifying hardware development will make robotics more accessible and encourage wider adoption of purpose-built systems:

We believe that a robot with purpose-built hardware designed for a specific task will do that task faster, cheaper and more reliably than any general purpose robot ever could, regardless of which model runs on it.

By the end of 2027, coprod plans to have its complete component range commercially available, qualified, certified and packaged. Large-scale production is expected to take place in Shenzhen and Texas, while the company's headquarters, core team and research and development operations will remain in Switzerland.

The new funding will support the commercial launch of coprod's first hardware components and the development of a prototyping facility in Lausanne. Equipped with CNC machinery, lasers and electronic assembly and testing equipment, the facility is expected to reduce development cycles from two weeks to 24 hours.

It will also enable the company to provide detailed technical documentation and digital twin models for its components, helping improve the transition from simulation to real-world robotic applications.

The announcement comes as Europe’s leading policymakers, founders and investors gather at Slush in Helsinki to discuss the state of EU Inc. After two years of campaigning for a single European company standard, EU–INC and Startups for Europe remain strong supporters of the European Commission’s original proposal.

The Commission delivered a solid framework that could finally give European founders a genuine alternative to incorporating in Delaware, and allow companies to start and scale under one common European standard.

But the Council’s negotiating mandate of 19 October has weakened or removed some of the very provisions that would make EU Inc a true European standard:

  • Free choice of registration – Weakened: Founders can choose where to incorporate, but national authorities have more room to challenge that choice in certain circumstances, creating legal uncertainty.
  • Employee stock options – Restricted: The scheme stops at 750 employees or €150 million in turnover, excluding successful scale-ups where ESOPs are most valuable.
  • Central EU register – Removed: The 27 national registers remain, preserving the fragmentation EU Inc was meant to overcome.
  • Simplified insolvency – Removed: Different insolvency rules across Member States make winding down a company harder, costlier and less predictable for investors.

The demand for a single European company standard is clear.

In September, President von der Leyen warned against turning EU Inc from a speedboat into a heavy tanker. EU–INC and Startups for Europe say that warning is now becoming true.

The organisations judge EU Inc by one simple test: Would a founder choose it over a Delaware C-Corp?

The Commission's original proposal passes that test.

The Council's mandate does not.

EU–INC and Startups for Europe warn that proceeding directly to final negotiations, known as trilogues, risks further compromises rather than restoring the provisions already lost. If the proposal continues on its current course, Europe risks adopting an EU Inc that founders won't use.

Andreas Klinger, Co-Initiator of EU–INC and investor, warns that the consequences go far beyond the regulation itself:

“Founders don't need a European regulation that delivers on paper but fails in practice.

They need a company structure that makes it easier to build, raise capital and scale across Europe. The Commission's original proposal delivers that. But if we strip away the things that make it work, founders will simply incorporate elsewhere. We have one chance to get EU Inc right, and we can’t waste it.

We risk more than Europe's competitiveness. We risk losing the trust of an entire generation of founders who still believe they can build global companies in Europe.”

A call to Member States to change course – and get EU Inc right

EU–INC and Startups for Europe are asking the Commission to withdraw, negotiate, and re-table its original proposal. Not to abandon EU Inc, but to give it the time and chance to succeed.

The call follows a joint letter to Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, in which both organisations reaffirm their strong support for the Commission's original proposal and call for Member States to reconsider their positions.

For Simon Schaefer, President of Startups for Europe and Co-Initiator EU-INC, the responsibility now lies with Member States to put Europe's collective interests ahead of national compromises:

“A truly European company standard requires Member States to look beyond their national interests. We cannot spend years negotiating one of Europe's most important competitiveness reforms only to end up with another patchwork of national rules.

This is an opportunity for Member States to reconsider their positions and make sure EU Inc delivers on its original promise.”

Backed by more than 26,000 EU–INC co-signatories, the campaign remains committed to its original mission: One Europe. One Standard. One that founders can actually use.

]]> https://tech.eu/2026/11/19/eu-inc-calls-on-von-der-leyen-to-withdraw-and-re-table-eu-inc-proposal/ Thu, 19 Nov 2026 13:00:00 +0000 https://tech.eu/2026/11/19/eu-inc-calls-on-von-der-leyen-to-withdraw-and-re-table-eu-inc-proposal/feed 0 true <![CDATA[€100B in company value, one shared ambition: European tech leaders demand political reform at Slush]]> https://tech.eu/2026/11/19/100b-in-company-value-one-shared-ambition-european-tech-leaders-demand-political-reform-at-slush/ https://tech.eu/2026/11/19/100b-in-company-value-one-shared-ambition-european-tech-leaders-demand-political-reform-at-slush/#comments More than 35 European tech founders and business leaders issued a joint declaration at Slush 2026, calling for three fundamental shifts in European technology policy to strengthen the continent's global competitiveness. Representing more than €100 billion in company value and 115,000 jobs, the signatories pledged their long-term commitment to building and scaling technology companies in Europe.

“We share one conviction: Europe can lead the next era of technology, and we want to make it happen.”

The declaration challenges the prevailing narrative of European decline, pointing to the continent's scientific excellence, private wealth and strengths in advanced manufacturing, energy, aerospace, robotics, quantum, climate technology and AI. The EU accounts for around 22 per cent of global scientific publications, compared with 17 per cent for the US, according to the declaration. Yet Europe has struggled to translate these strengths into global technology leadership.

“Europe was never short of talent, technology or capital. It was short of the political determination and the boldness to put them to work.”

The signatories identify three political priorities to address this imbalance.

Mobilising European capital to fund technology growth

The declaration argues that Europe's investment challenges stem not from a shortage of capital but from how it is allocated. European households alone hold more than €12 trillion in savings, alongside substantial pools of capital managed by pension funds and institutional investors.

However, much of this wealth finances innovation and infrastructure overseas, while European technology companies struggle to secure large growth rounds domestically.

“Europe funds the earliest, riskiest phase of deep tech and research-backed innovation – and then foreign capital steps in and captures the growth. This must end.”

The signatories call for the accelerated implementation of the Savings and Investments Union, alongside investment in critical technology infrastructure, including access to frontier AI and greater European compute capacity.

“European savings should finance European innovation, and European citizens should participate in the wealth it creates.”

Completing the Single Market through EU Inc

Despite the scale of Europe's Single Market, founders continue to face fragmented corporate, tax and employment rules when expanding across member states.

The declaration identifies EU Inc, an optional, digital-first European company structure, as a critical first step towards removing these barriers. It would enable founders to incorporate once and operate across member states without establishing separate local entities, while harmonising employee share options and investment processes.

“A startup founded in Paris, Berlin, Warsaw or Milan should be able to hire, raise capital, sell and scale across the continent as easily as an American company expands across the United States.”

The signatories also advocate for deeper integration of European capital markets, including the creation of a pan-European stock exchange.

“The objective is one market, one rulebook and one launchpad for global companies.”

Simplifying regulation while protecting competition

The declaration takes a dual approach to regulation, calling for reduced administrative burdens alongside stronger enforcement of competition rules. It argues that excessive regulation and the abuse of market power by dominant technology platforms are both significant barriers to European innovation.

“The re-establishment of fair digital competition and smart simplification are not opposing agendas but two sides of the same coin.”

The signatories call for policymakers to prioritise reducing red tape, particularly in fast-moving sectors such as AI, while enforcing the Digital Markets Act (DMA) to prevent dominant platforms from restricting access to critical digital markets. They argue that fair competition could enable European companies that are already competitive under existing conditions to emerge as global leaders.

European founders pledge to double down on Europe

The declaration concludes with a commitment to work with the European Commission and national governments to translate these priorities into policy. The signatories frame technological leadership as fundamental not only to economic prosperity but also to democratic resilience and political independence.

“We bring the experience of those building Europe’s technological sovereignty and competitiveness every day, and we are prepared to double down on Europe. We call on Europe’s political leaders to match this ambition.”

"Europe should be the best place in the world to start and build a global-scale tech company"

Europe should be the best place in the world to start and build a global-scale tech company. We can be, if we really want to."

Signatory Naren Shaam, Omio Group’s Founder and CEO, shared:

“Europe has the talent to build global tech leaders. Now policymakers need to make scaling easier: more European growth capital, a single market that works in practice, and simpler tech rules alongside firm competition enforcement.

We chose to build in Europe. Europe should make it easier for companies like ours to grow globally.”

Follow through here matters enormously for every European company trying to compete on a level playing field. We chose to build in Europe, and we are ready to double down. Now we need Europe to match that ambition with consistent enforcement. That is how this continent stops playing defence and starts leading.”

The largest funding rounds reflected this diversity, spanning workplace productivity, financial decision-making, autonomous driving, healthcare technology and enterprise compliance.

The UK and Germany accounted for many of the largest transactions, while France, Belgium, the Netherlands and Nordic countries also contributed to investment activity. Funding remained concentrated in a relatively small number of substantial rounds, alongside numerous smaller investments across different markets and software segments.

AI played an increasingly prominent role in shaping investment trends, particularly in enterprise automation and specialised business applications. At the same time, continued funding for cybersecurity, compliance and developer infrastructure demonstrated sustained investor interest in software addressing broader operational and business needs.

For further insights into funding trends across the European technology ecosystem, explore Tech.eu's Funding Explorer, which is free and open to everyone.

Here are the European software companies that raised the most funding in H1 2026.


Amount raised in H1 2026: $125M London-based Granola develops an AI-powered notepad that helps professionals capture, organise and use information from meetings. The application works with video conferencing platforms, including Zoom, Google Meet and Microsoft Teams, transforming conversations into structured notes and making meeting context accessible for subsequent work. Its tools support individual productivity and knowledge sharing across teams. The investment will support further product development and scaling, including the expansion of its capabilities for businesses.

Its software enables businesses to build, deploy and manage automated decision-making workflows for credit underwriting, fraud detection, customer onboarding and insurance claims. The platform combines AI agents with decision controls designed to support complex processes in regulated environments. In June 2026, Taktile secured $110 million in Series C funding, led by Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives. The capital will support product development, expansion of its engineering teams and international growth, including Latin America.

Rather than focusing on passenger transport, Oxa targets repetitive driving operations in ports, airports, warehouses and manufacturing facilities, where autonomous vehicles can support industrial workflows. In March 2026, Oxa raised $103 million in Series D funding, including investment from the UK's National Wealth Fund, NVentures and bp Ventures. The funding will support expanded deployments with existing customers and the introduction of its autonomous technology into additional industrial projects.


Amount raised in H1 2026: $100M Helping businesses manage sustainability and regulatory requirements, Mannheim-based osapiens offers an enterprise software platform that brings compliance, sustainability management and operational processes together. In June 2026, Conduct raised $60 million in Series A funding to support the expansion of its engineering and go-to-market teams, including hiring in the US.


Amount raised in H1 2026: $60M Applying AI to real estate law, Orbital develops software that automates document-intensive legal processes involved in property transactions. Its platform serves law firms, in-house legal teams, developers, title companies and real estate investment trusts across residential and commercial property markets. Amount raised in H1 2026: $50M Stockholm-based Endra develops AI-powered engineering software that automates the design of mechanical, electrical and plumbing (MEP) systems in buildings. In June 2026, Endra raised $50 million in Series A funding led by Andreessen Horowitz, with participation from Notion Capital and Norrsken VC. Amount raised in H1 2026: $50M SolveAI develops an AI-powered platform that enables employees to create enterprise software without coding. Its platform uses specialised AI agents to handle different stages of software development, from initial proposals and technical specifications to frontend and backend development, while maintaining enterprise security and compliance standards.
